SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r3.claim: Al-Anam addresses people already poor and promises parents provision first; al-Isra addresses those fearing future poverty and promises children provision first to reassure them that children will not diminish their means.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r3.anchor: فأجبت البلاغةُ تقديمَ عِدَتِهم بالرزق تكميل العِدَةِ برزق الأولاد

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p42/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p42/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p42/r1.claim: Al-An‘am addresses parents already poor and promises their provision first; al-Isra addresses those fearing future poverty and puts children first, assuring them each child has provision and will not consume theirs.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p42/r1.anchor: فهم يقتلون أولادهم من الفقر الواقع بهم لا أنهم يخشونه فأوجبت البلاغة تقديم عدتهم بالرزق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p493/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p493/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p493/r1.claim: In 6:151, parents are currently poor, so their provision is named first; in 17:31, the wealthy fear future poverty, so the children’s provision comes first to reassure them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p493/r1.anchor: فهم يقتلون أولادهم من الفقر الواقع بهم لا أنهم يخشونه فأوجبت البلاغة تقديم عِدتهم بالرزق تكميل العدة برزق الأولاد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p956/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p956/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p956/r1.claim: For parents poor at present, God first assures their provision; for parents merely fearing future poverty, He names the children’s provision first to show they bring provision with them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p956/r1.anchor: فلما كانوا مفتقرين فهم محتاجون للرزق لعيلوا أنفسهم ثم أولادهم لذا بدأ تعالى برزقهم هم أولاً

BURHAN:v3p284/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p284/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p284/r6.claim: For poor parents in 6:151, their own provision comes first; for the wealthy addressed in 17:31, children's provision is the concern, so it comes first there.
BURHAN:v3p284/r6.anchor: قدم المخاطبين في الأولى دون الثانية لأن الخطاب في الأولى في الفقراء بدليل قوله ﴿ من إملاق ﴾

STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.speaker: Some early authorities
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.claim: Some early authorities considered certain verses, possibly those listed, to have been revealed in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.anchor: Some early authorities, however, considered certain verses, perhaps vv. 20, 23, 91, 93, 114, 141, and 151–53, to have been revealed in Madinah

BURSEVI:v3p90/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90/r1.claim: The command “come” first meant an invitation from a higher place to a lower one, then broadened to any invitation to approach.
BURSEVI:v3p90/r1.anchor: {تعالوا} أمر من تعالى والأصل فيه أن يقوله من في مكان عال لمن هو أسفل منه

BURSEVI:v3p90/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90/r2.claim: “Recite” answers the command to come and means “read”; the prohibitions are the verses that follow.
BURSEVI:v3p90/r2.anchor:
{اتل} جواب الأمر أي : أقرأ.
{ما حرم ربكم} أي : الذي حرمه ربكم أي الآيات المشتملة عليه.

BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.claim: These three verses contain ten comprehensive duties, unchanged across revealed books, peoples, and eras; whoever practices them enters Paradise, while whoever abandons them enters Hell.
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.anchor: هذه الآيات الثلاث إلى قوله : {لعلكم تتقون} تشتمل على عشر خصال جامعة للخير كله لم ينسخهن شيء

BURSEVI:v3p90/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90/r4.claim: The first duty is avoiding shirk, the chief prohibition, since God accepts no worship alongside it; it includes overt idol worship and inwardly recognizing anything alongside God.
BURSEVI:v3p90/r4.anchor: قدم الشرك لأنه رأس المحرمات ، ولا يقبل الله تعالى معه شيئا من الطاعات وهو ينقسم إلى جلي وخفي

BURSEVI:v3p90/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90/r5.claim: A Persian verse urges the troubled poet to write the declaration of unity on the page of all else.
BURSEVI:v3p90/r5.anchor:
تادم وحدت زدى حافظ شوريده حال
خامه توحيد كش برورق اين

BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r1.claim: Doing good to parents necessarily forbids mistreatment; positive wording emphasizes that merely avoiding abuse does not fulfill their rights.
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r1.anchor: {وبالوالدين إحسانا} أي : وأحسنوا بهما إحسانا ، أي : لا تسيئوا إليهما لأن المحرم هو الإساءة

BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r2.claim: Filial duty follows the prohibition of shirk because parents are the immediate means of one’s existence; neglecting their rights is the greatest sin after shirk.
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r2.anchor: لأن الوالدين سببان قريبان لوجوده كما أن الله تعالى موجده فالتقاعد عن أداء حقوقهما عقوق

BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r3.speaker: بعض الأولياء
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r3.claim: A holy man says that serving his mother enabled him to meet al-Khiḍr in the wilderness of the Israelites.
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r3.anchor: كنت في تيه بني إسرائيل ، فإذا رجل يماشيني فتعجبت منه وألهمت أنه الخضر

BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r4.claim: The Persian verse depicts Paradise as lying beneath mothers’ feet.
BURSEVI:v3p90#2/r4.anchor:
جنت كه سراى ما درانست
زير قد مات ما درانست

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r1.claim: The ban includes burying daughters alive from poverty; imlāq means depleted provisions and expenses.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r1.anchor:
{ولا تقتلوا أولادكم} أي : لا تدفنوا بناتكم حية {من إملاق} من أجل فقر.
والإملاق
117
نفاد الزاد

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r2.claim: God, rather than the parents, provides for them and their children, so fear of poverty is no excuse.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r2.anchor: {نحن نرزقكم وإياهم} لا أنتم فلا تخافوا الفقر بناء على عجزكم عن تحصيل الرزق.

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r3.claim: This third duty forbids destroying God’s creation, cutting off descendants, and failing to trust His provision, which amounts to denying His promise in 11:6.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الحكم الثالث من الأحكام العشرة ، وإنما حرم قتل الأولاد لما فيه من هدم بنيان الله

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r4.claim: A Persian couplet counsels preserving dignity through poverty and contentment, since provision is already apportioned.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r4.anchor:
ما آبروى فقر وقناعت نمى بريم
جزء : 3 رقم الصفحة : 115
با ادشه بكوى كه

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r5.claim: The fourth duty forbids fornication in its forms: public brothels and secret liaisons; forbidding approach intensifies the ban.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r5.anchor: {ولا تقربوا الفواحش} أي : الزنى وجيء بصيغة الجمع قصدا إلى النهي عن أنواعها

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r6.claim: Inwardly, the ban covers acts and intentions that distance one from Paradise or truth, and even illicit looking.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r6.anchor: ويدخل في ذلك ما يبعده من الجنة ويدنيه من النار ، وهو ما ظهر وما

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Satan tempts men and women through three bodily stations, including eyes and hearts and their sexual parts.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : "أن الشيطان من الرجل في ثلاثة منازل في عينيه وفي قلبه

BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r8.claim: The fifth duty protects anyone made inviolable by Islam or covenant, except where law authorizes death for apostasy, adultery after marriage, or murder.
BURSEVI:v3p90#3/r8.anchor: عصمها بالإسلام أو بالعهد فيخرج منها الحربي {إلا بالحق}

BURSEVI:v3p91/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
BURSEVI:v3p91/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Kharrāz says a dead, handsome youth smiled and told him that lovers remain alive after death, merely moving from one home to another.
BURSEVI:v3p91/r1.anchor: كنت بمكة فجزت يوما بباب بني شيبة ، فرأيت شابا حسن الوجه ميتا فنظرت في وجهه فتبسم

BURSEVI:v3p91/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91/r2.claim: “That” refers to the five duties just listed, which God emphatically enjoined so people would use reason to restrain their souls from them.
BURSEVI:v3p91/r2.anchor:
{ذالكم} إشارة إلى ما ذكر من التكاليف الخمسة.
{وصاكم به} أي : أمركم ربكم بحفظه أمرا مؤكدا.

BURSEVI:v3p91/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91/r4.claim: Inwardly, the true killing is to die in pursuit of God; one killed in His path remains alive with Him.
BURSEVI:v3p91/r4.anchor: والإشارة : أن القتل الحق هو القتل في طلب الحق والمقتول في سبيل الله هو حي عند ربه.

QASHANI:6:151/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:151/r1.claim: Idolatry is serving whim and Satan; idolaters make whim their ruler in deciding lawful and forbidden things, so God's commands must govern.
QASHANI:6:151/r1.anchor: إذ الشرك في نفسه ليس إلا عبادة الهوى والشيطان.

QASHANI:6:151/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:151/r2.claim: Because the dispute concerns banning wholesome things, God lists prohibitions to indicate permissions and enumerates vices to convey virtues, beginning with the rational faculty's greatest vice.
QASHANI:6:151/r2.anchor: ولما كان الكلام معهم في تحريم الطيبات عدد المحرمات ليستدل بها على المحللات

QASHANI:6:151/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:151/r3.claim: Association reflects faulty reasoning and failure to use intellect or recognize proof; honoring parents follows knowledge of God because they are proximate causes of existence and nurture.
QASHANI:6:151/r3.anchor: إذ الشرك من خطئها في النظر وقصورها عن استعمال العقل ودرك البرهان

QASHANI:6:151/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:6:151/r4.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that obeying one's parents is obedience to God and His Messenger; Qashani gives no grading.
QASHANI:6:151/r4.anchor: من أطاع الوالدين فقد أطاع الله ورسوله

QASHANI:6:151/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:151/r5.claim: Disobedience to parents follows association in severity; ignorance of their rights comes from ignorance of God's rights and attributes.
QASHANI:6:151/r5.anchor: فعقوقهما يلي الشرك ولا يقع الجهل بحقوقهما إلا عن الجهل بحقوق الله تعالى

QASHANI:6:151/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:151/r6.claim: Killing children for poverty reflects ignorance that God provides for every creature; public indecencies are outward vice, while intention, desire, and concealment are inward vice.
QASHANI:6:151/r6.anchor: ثم بالنهي عن قتل الأولاد خشية الفقر، فإن ارتكاب ذلك لا يكون إلا عن الجهل والعمى

QASHANI:6:151/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:151/r7.claim: Fornication, wine, and usury are outward indecencies; their hidden forms include intending them, desiring them, and secretly stealing or committing prohibited acts.
QASHANI:6:151/r7.anchor: من الأعمال القبيحة الشنيعة عند العقل

QASHANI:6:151#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:151#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:151#2/r1.claim: The prohibition on killing a protected soul addresses the predatory faculty's vice; lawful killing is by retaliation or disbelief, and only the rational avoid these vices.
QASHANI:6:151#2/r1.anchor: أي: بالقصاص والكفر، وختم الكلام بقوله

SULAMI:v1p216#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p216#3/r1.speaker: حارث المحاسبي
SULAMI:v1p216#3/r1.claim: The inward indecencies are actions intended for someone other than God.
SULAMI:v1p216#3/r1.anchor: قال حارث المحاسبي : الفواحش ما أريد به غير الله

SULAMI:v1p216#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p216#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p216#3/r2.claim: Outward indecency is ostentation in deeds, while inward indecency is making false spiritual claims.
SULAMI:v1p216#3/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : ما ظهر من الفواحش في الأفعال هو الرياء ، وما بطن منها الدعاوي الكاذبة

TUSTARI:6:151/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:151/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:151/r1.claim: Outward indecencies are acts forbidden to the limbs; inward indecency is persistence, either continuing a sin or inwardly loving it while unable to act but ready if able.
TUSTARI:6:151/r1.anchor: ما ظهر منها ما نهى عن إتيانه بالجوارح الظاهرة، وما بطن يعني الإصرار عليه هو على ضربين:

TUSTARI:6:151/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:151/r2.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:6:151/r2.claim: Eating lawful food out of craving counts as persistence in sin; carrying one's present state into tomorrow without reaching tomorrow also counts as persistence.
TUSTARI:6:151/r2.anchor: وقال سهل: من أكل الحلال بالشهوة فهو مصر، ومن جاوز حاله إلى الغد ما لم يأت الغد فهو مصر.

TUSTARI:6:151/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:151/r3.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:6:151/r3.claim: Prophets may perform outward actions for which they later repent, so thoughts about irrelevant matters are even more possible.
TUSTARI:6:151/r3.anchor: وقال سهل: من أكل الحلال بالشهوة فهو مصر، ومن جاوز حاله إلى الغد ما لم يأت الغد فهو مصر. فسئل عن الأنبياء

TUSTARI:6:151/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:151/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:151/r4.claim: The heart has an obligatory act of worship of its own: stillness.
TUSTARI:6:151/r4.anchor: قيل له: هل للقلب من تعبد استعبده الله به دون الجوارح؟ فقال: نعم سكون القلب.

TUSTARI:6:151/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:151/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:151/r5.claim: Stillness is knowledge that leads to certainty, and stillness joined with certainty is obligatory.
TUSTARI:6:151/r5.anchor: قيل له: السكون هو الغرض أم العلم الذي به السكون؟ فقال: هو علم اسميه السكون، يجر ذلك السكون إلى اليقين

MAJAZ:v1p208/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p208/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p208/r4.claim: إملاق means loss of one's property and poverty; أملق فلان means his wealth went away, like أقفر.
MAJAZ:v1p208/r4.anchor: من ذهاب ما فى أيديكم يقال: أملق فلان

NAHHAS:v2p106/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r1.claim: ما حرم ربكم is accusative as the object of حرم.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r1.anchor: ما حرم ربكم عليكم ) ( ما ) في موضع نصب بالفعل

NAHHAS:v2p106/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r2.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p106/r2.claim: Al-Farra prefers taking لا in ألا تشركوا as a prohibition because the next command also uses prohibition.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r2.anchor: الفراء يختار أن يكون ( لا ) للنهي لأن بعده ( ولا تقتلوا

NAHHAS:v2p106/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r3.claim: Alternatively, أن may be accusative in apposition to ما, a purpose phrase meaning dislike, or nominative meaning “it is that you not associate.”
NAHHAS:v2p106/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون أن في موضع نصب بدلا من ما أي أتل عليكم تحريم الإشراك

NAHHAS:v2p106/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r4.claim: إحسانا is a verbal noun; إملاق means fear of poverty; ما ظهر منها وما بطن is apposition to الفواحش.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r4.anchor: وبالوالدين إحسانا ) مصدر ( ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق ) أي من خوف الفقر

NAHHAS:v2p106/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r5.claim: ذلكم وصاكم به can mean “that is the command” or that God has clarified and commanded it.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r5.anchor: ذلكم وصاكم به ) أي الأمر ذلك ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى بين لكم وصاكم به

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r1.claim: The Prophet's final testament is recited in these commands through 6:153.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله انه قال : من سره ان ينظر إلى وصية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التي عليها خاتمة ، فليقرا : قل تعالوا اتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r2.claim: These three verses are the decisive commands.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : هن الايات المحكمات : قل تعالوا اتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم ثلاث آيات .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ، عبادة بن الصامت
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r3.claim: The Prophet enjoined seven traits, beginning with not associating anything with God even under torture.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r3.anchor: عن عبادة الصامت قال : اوصانا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسبع خصال ، الا تشركوا بالله شيئا وان حرقتم وقطعتم وصلبتم .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r4.claim: Honoring parents includes speaking truth and fulfilling their rights.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1414/r4.anchor: في قول الله : وبالوالدين احسانا ، قال : قولوا صدقا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r1.claim: A report calls asking people for help one of the prohibited indecencies.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن عبيد ان أبا حازم الرهاوي حدثه ان سمع مولاه يقول : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : مسالة الناس من الفواحش .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r2.speaker: يحيى بن جابر
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r2.claim: One indecency is divorcing a woman after she miscarries his child without any suspicion against her.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r2.anchor: عن يحيى بن جابر قال : بلغني ان من الفواحش التي نهى الله عنها في كتابة تزويج الرجل المراة ، فاذا نفضت له ولدها طلقها من غير ريبة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r3.speaker: محمد بن قيس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r3.claim: The verse addresses people who used to walk around the House naked.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس ، في قول الله تعالى : ولا تقربوا الفواحش قال : كانوا يمشون حول البيت عراة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : الفواحش يعني : الزنا .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء، عكرمة، أبو صالح، علي بن حسين، قتادة، الربيع بن أنس، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r5.claim: Pre-Islamic people tolerated secret adultery but disapproved of it publicly; God prohibited both.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r6.claim: An alternative reading identifies apparent indecencies as marriage to one's mother or daughter.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس : الفواحش ما ظهر منها قال : نكاح الامهات والبنات وروى عن سعيد بن جبير نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r7.claim: Apparent indecencies include marrying women one's fathers married and marrying two sisters together.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1415/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد : اما ما ظهر منها فقوله : ولا تنكحوا ما نكح اباؤكم ، وقوله : وان تجمعوا بين الاختين .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r1.claim: Apparent indecencies may mean wronging people.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة : ما ظهر منها : الظلم ظلم الناس .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r2.speaker: الزهري
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r2.claim: Another interpretation is nakedness during pre-Islamic circumambulation.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r2.anchor: عن الزهري ، في قوله : الفواحش ما ظهر منها ، قال : العري ، وكانوا يطوفون بالبيت عراة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، قتادة، عطاء الخراساني، الربيع بن أنس، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ، قال : ما بطن السر ، وروى عن عكرمة وقتادة وعطاء الخرساني والربيع بن انس والسدي نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، الزهري، مجاهد، محمد بن قيس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r4.claim: An alternative identifies hidden indecencies specifically as secret adultery.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ، قال : ما بطن الزنا . وروى عن الزهري ومجاهد ومحمد بن قيس نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r5.speaker: علي بن حسين
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r5.claim: Another view takes hidden indecency to mean marrying one's father's wife.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r5.anchor: عن علي بن حسين : ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن قال : ما بطن : نكاح امراة الاب .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r6.claim: Hidden indecencies include adultery and theft.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة : وما بطن من الفواحش : الزنا والسرقة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r7.claim: The soul forbidden to kill means the life of a believer.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله تعالى : ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله الا بالحق ، يعني : نفس المؤمن .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r8.claim: The exception concerns a life otherwise forbidden to kill, unless there is a rightful cause.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r8.anchor: وبه عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم قتلها الا بالحق .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r9.speaker: النبي ﷺ، عبادة بن الصامت
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r9.claim: The Prophet pledged people to these commands; fulfillment earns reward, while violations may be punished here or left to God in the Hereafter.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r9.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ايكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الايات الثلاث ؟ ثم تلا : قل تعالوا اتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r10.speaker: النبي ﷺ، عبادة بن الصامت
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r10.claim: Those who fulfill the pledge are rewarded; violations may be punished in this life or left to God's will in the Hereafter.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1416/r10.anchor: ومن وفي بهن اجره الله ، ومن انتقص منهن شيئا فادركه الله في الدنيا كانت عقوبة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : وصية الله : دين الله .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.claim: The three linked groups are social order opened by avoiding shirk, interpersonal and economic order opened by protecting orphan property, and the comprehensive principle of following Islam's straight path and avoiding deviant paths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.anchor: إلى ثلاثة أقسام : الأول : أحكام بها إصلاح الحالة الاجتماعية العامة بين الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.claim: Each of the three sections is closed with a testament from God, repeated three times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.anchor: وقد ذيل كل قسم من هذه الأقسام بالوصاية به بقوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r1.claim: The prohibitions use both negative commands and explicit or implied positive commands, since commanding an act also forbids its opposite; he says the reason for varying forms will be explained later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r1.anchor: لأن الأمر بالشيء يقتضي النهي عن ضده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r2.claim: An is explanatory of the recitation because reciting includes saying; the clause against associating partners is an appositional explanation, and it comes first because sound belief opens reform and success.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r2.anchor: والابتداء بالنهي عن الإشراك لأن إصلاح الاعتقاد هو مفتاح باب الإصلاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r3.claim: Ihsanan is a verbal noun standing for its verb, commanding kindness to parents and thereby forbidding abuse; the positive formulation honors parents and recalls Arab harshness toward aging fathers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r3.anchor: و { إحسانا } مصدر ناب مناب فعله ، أي وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r4.claim: The command to treat parents well is counted among prohibitions because the prohibited act is mistreating them; the Quran repeatedly directs children to show them ihsan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p157/r4.anchor: وبذلك الاعتبار وقع هنا في عداد ما حرم الله لأن المحرم هو الإساءة للوالدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r1.claim: In this verse, poverty is the actual present cause of infanticide; elsewhere the Quran also forbids killing children from fear of future poverty, and Arabs buried daughters through inability or anticipation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r1.anchor: والإملاق : الفقر ، وكونه علة لقتل الأولاد يقع على وجهين : أن يكون حاصلا بالفعل ، وهو المراد هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r2.speaker: إسحاق بن خلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r2.claim: His poem depicts a father dreading that poverty will expose his daughter's body to hardship, illustrating fear of future poverty as a motive for infanticide.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r2.anchor:
قال إسحاق بن خلف ، وهو إسلامي قديم :
إذا تذكرت بنتي حين تندبني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r3.claim: The promise of provision interrupts the prohibition and refutes poverty as an excuse: God provided for children, so a father should earn for them rather than kill them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r3.anchor: علة للنهي عن قتلهم ، إبطالا لمعذرتهم : لأن الفقر قد جعلوه عذرا لقتل الأولاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r4.claim: The speech shifts from speaking of the Lord in the third person to God's first-person voice, making God seem to speak directly and confirming the Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r4.anchor: إلى طريق التكلم بضمير : نرزقكم تذكيرا بالذي أمر بهذا القول كله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r5.claim: Parents are mentioned before their children because God has sustained the parents without their starving; poverty afflicted the parents, not the children.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p158/r5.anchor: وقدم رزق الآباء للإشارة إلى أنه كما رزق الآباء ، فلم يموتوا جوعا ، كذلك يرزق الأبناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r1.claim: Fronting the subject in the provision clause conveys exclusivity: God provides for parents and children, while parents provide for neither themselves nor their children.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r1.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على المسند الفعلي . هنا لإفادة الاختصاص : أي نحن نرزقكم وإياهم لا أنتم ترزقون أنفسكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r2.claim: The prohibition against approaching indecencies warns more forcefully than forbidding their commission; proximity implies even slight involvement, a metaphorical extension because sins have no literal location.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r2.anchor: وقد نهى عن القرب منها ، وهو أبلغ في التحذير من النهي عن ملابستها : لأن القرب من الشيء مظنة الوقوع فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r3.claim: Indecencies are major sins involving harmful consequences; public examples include anger and slander, while hidden examples chiefly include adultery and theft, common among Arabs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r3.anchor: والفواحش : الآثام الكبيرة ، وهي المشتملة على مفاسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r4.claim: He interprets indecencies specifically as adultery: public sexual acts in brothels and private illicit lovers as the hidden form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r4.anchor: ومن المفسرين من فسر الفواحش بالزنا ، وجعل ما ظهر منها ما يفعله سفهاؤهم في الحوانيت وديار البغايا ، وبما بطن اتخاذ الأخدان سرا ، وروي هذا عن السدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r5.speaker: الضحاك وابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r5.claim: They report that pre-Islamic Arabs treated secret adultery as permissible but disapproved of it publicly, so God prohibited both forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r5.anchor: وروي عن الضحاك وابن عباس : كان أهل الجاهلية يرون الزنا سرا حلالا ، ويستقبحونه في العلانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r6.claim: The plural indecencies favors the broad meaning of major sins; the similar list in al-Isra does not require both passages to mean only adultery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159/r6.anchor: وعندي أن صيغة الجمع في الفواحش ترجح التفسير الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r1.claim: The distinction between what is apparent and concealed was explained earlier in the same surah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r1.anchor: وتقدم القول في : { ما ظهر منها وما بطن } عند قوله تعالى : { وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r2.claim: Killing is singled out as a grave, widespread indecency under the broad interpretation; the generic definite soul encompasses all persons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r2.anchor: وأعقب ذلك بالنهي عن قتل النفس ، وهو من الفواحش على تفسيرها بالأعم ، تخصيصا له بالذكر : لأنه فساد عظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r3.claim: Describing the soul as forbidden emphasizes that its prohibition is ancient, dating from Adam; attaching prohibition to a person means prohibition of killing that person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r3.anchor: تأكيدا للتحريم بأنه تحريم قديم فإن الله حرم قتل النفس من عهد آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r4.claim: Alternatively, the wording may mean God made the soul inviolable; the author cites the sacred precinct and a hadith about what lies between Medina's lava fields.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p160/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى : { حرم الله } جعلها الله حرما أي شيئا محترما لا يعتدى عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r1.claim: The exception covers every circumstance of killing: no killing is allowed except for a cause established as rightful under sound reason and the relevant law; the preposition marks circumstance or cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r1.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من عموم أحوال ملابسة القتل ، أي لا تقتلوها في أية حالة أو بأي سبب تنتحلونه إلا بسبب الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r2.claim: In Islamic usage, rightful killing includes combatants and retaliation established by the Quran, plus apostasy after seeking repentance, adultery by a married person, and persistent refusal of prayer after its time, based on hadiths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r2.anchor: وقد فصل الإسلام حق قتل النفس بالقرآن والسنة ، وهو قتل المحارب والقصاص ، وهذان بنص القرآن ، وقتل المرتد عن الإسلام بعد استتابته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r3.claim: Other lawful cases include killing in authorized defense, rebels and zakat-refusers; jihad itself is outside this exception, though killing a prisoner for a valid interest can be rightful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r3.anchor: فيه شرعا وذلك قتل من يقتل من البغاة وهو بنص القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r4.claim: The singular demonstrative refers collectively to all the preceding commands; a plural demonstrative would also be idiomatic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p161/r4.anchor: والإشارة بقوله : { ذلكم وصاكم به } إلى مجموع ما ذكر ، ولذلك أفرد اسم الإشارة باعتبار المذكور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r1.claim: The wish that people reason means they should become rational: committing these prohibitions shows such debased judgment that offenders seem mindless.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r1.anchor: أي يصيروا ذوي عقول لأن ملابسة بعض هذه المحرمات ينبىء عن خساسة عقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r2.claim: The closing sentence marks the end of prohibitions concerned with social order: right belief, family stability, avoiding corruption, and preserving life by ending mutual killing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162/r2.anchor: فأومأ إلى تنهية نوع من المحرمات وهو المحرمات الراجع تحريمها إلى إصلاح الحالة الاجتماعية للأمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r1.claim: God commands the Prophet to call all people to hear the prohibitions of Islam, the message sent to all humanity; taʿālaw means come, from elevation, and the reciprocal form conveys the caller’s raising of the addressee.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r1.anchor: هذا أمر من الله عز وجل لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدعوا جميع الخلق إلى سماع تلاوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r2.claim: Atlu means to recite in sequence; mā is its object and a relative pronoun. Al-Zajjaj instead suspends atlu and makes mā the object of ḥarrama, a construction the author calls strained.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r2.anchor: وأتل معناه اسردوا نص من التلاوة التي يصح هي اتباع بعض الحروف بعضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r3.claim: An lā tushrikū can be a nominative clause with an omitted subject or an accusative apposition to mā; a purpose reading would remove it from the recited prohibitions, so the intended prohibition is jussive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r3.anchor: أن تكون في موضع رفع الابتداء التقدير، الأمر أن أو ذلك أن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r4.claim: Reading tushrikū as a subjunctive governed by an is possible, but the author says its jussive prohibitive sense is the intended one; an may connect to either subjunctive or command and prohibition verbs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r4.anchor: وتشركوا يصح أن يكون منصوبا بأن، ويتوجه أن يكون مجزوما بالنهي وهو الصحيح في المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r5.claim: Shayʾan comprehensively means every worshipped thing besides God; iḥsānan is an absolute object with an elided command, show goodness to parents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r5.anchor: وشيئا عام يراد به كل معبود من دون الله، وإحسانا نصب على المصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r6.claim: The prohibitions can be grouped as associating partners, disobedience, approaching indecencies, and murder.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r6.anchor: والمحرمات تنفك من هذه المذكورات بالمعنى وهي الإشراك والعقوق وقرب الفواحش وقتل النفس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r7.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r7.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says these verses open the Torah, from the basmala through the end of the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r7.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: هذه الآيات مفتتح التوراة بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas calls these the unabrogated, decisive commandments shared by all revealed laws; others identify them as the Ten Commandments given to Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس هذه الآيات هي المحكمات التي ذكرها الله في سورة آل عمران

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r9.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r9.claim: Al-Tabari cites a verse of rajaz as evidence that an lā can govern a verb in the jussive when joined to the preceding prohibitions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p361#2/r9.anchor: وإن اعترض من قال إن تشركوا منصوب بأن بعطف المجزومات عليه فذلك موجود في كلام العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r1.claim: The command not to kill children addresses Arab infanticide and the word walad includes sons and daughters; imlāq means poverty or having no property.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r1.anchor: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم الآية نهي عن عادة العرب في وأد البنات، والولد يعم الذكر والأنثى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r2.claim: The author conjectures that imlāq may mean being left with only black stones, as at-raba and armal describe being left only with dust or sand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r2.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون معناه أملق أي لم يبق له إلا الملق كما قالوا أترب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r3.speaker: منذر بن سعيد وعلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r3.claim: Other glosses take imlāq as spending: Munḏir ibn Saʿid says expenditure, and a report has ʿAli telling a woman to spend as she wishes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r3.anchor: وذكر منذر بن سعيد أن الإملاق الإنفاق، ويقال أملق ماله بمعنى أنفقه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r4.speaker: محمد بن نعيم الترمذي ومؤرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r4.claim: Al-Naqqash transmits from Muhammad ibn Nuʿaym that imlāq is wasteful spending, and from Muʿarrij that it means hunger in the language of Lakhm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r4.anchor: وذكر النقاش عن محمد بن نعيم الترمذي أنه السرف في الإنفاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r5.speaker: السدي وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r5.claim: They restrict manifest indecency to public prostitution in brothels and hidden indecency to secret lovers; people condemned the public form alone, so both were forbidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r5.anchor: فقال السدي وابن عباس: ما ظهر هو زنا الحوانيت الشهير، وما بطن هو متخذات الأخدان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r6.claim: Mujahid offers specific readings of manifest and hidden indecency, including marriage to fathers’ wives and illicit sex; the author rejects such specifications as unsupported claims and keeps the general meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد ما ظهر هو نكاح حلائل الآباء ونحو ذلك، وما بطن هو الزنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r7.claim: The ban on killing covers Muslims and protected treaty-holders; the lawful exceptions are those set by sacred law, including apostasy, murder, adultery after marriage, and armed brigandage and related cases.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r7.anchor: تحريم قتل النفس المسلمة والمعاهدة، ومعنى الآية إلا بالحق الذي يوجب قتلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r8.claim: Dhālikum points to these prohibitions; waṣiyya is a firm, established command, as a poetic line about Muhammad’s counsel illustrates, and laʿallakum expresses hope from our perspective that reason will distinguish benefit from harm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362/r8.anchor: وذلكم إشارة إلى هذه المحرمات، و «الوصية» الأمر المؤكد المقرر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r1.claim: Mā means “that which.” The particle lā may be extra; if it is negative, the clause can mean “I recite to you the prohibition of associating partners.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r1.anchor: ما بمعنى الذي وفي لا قولان أحدهما أنها زائدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives another construal: “I advise you not to associate partners,” with the following command about parents understood as part of the same advice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r2.anchor: أن يكون المعنى أوصيكم أن لا تشركوا لأن قوله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r3.claim: If the sentence ends at “what your Lord prohibited,” Ibn al-Anbari takes ʿalaykum as an admonition: you must not associate partners.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنها إغراء كقوله ﴿ عليكم أنفسكم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r4.claim: The alternative construal takes ʿalaykum to mean that it is imposed and made obligatory upon you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r4.anchor: أن يكون بمعنى فرض عليكم ووجب عليكم أن لا تشركوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r5.claim: Shirk here is either claiming that God has a partner or obeying another in disobedience to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p147/r5.anchor: أنه ادعاء شريك مع الله عز وجل والثاني أنه طاعة غيره في معصيته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r1.claim: The ban on killing children refers to burying daughters alive; imlāq means fear of poverty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r1.anchor: يريد دفن البنات أحياء ﴿ من إملاق ﴾ أي من خوف فقر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi take the manifest and hidden indecencies as adultery done openly or secretly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r2.anchor: الزنا وما ظهر منه الإعلان به وما بطن الاستسرار به قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid say outward indecencies are wine and forbidden marriages, while hidden indecency is adultery.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r3.anchor: ما ظهر الخمر ونكاح المحرمات وما بطن الزنا قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the outward indecency is wine and the hidden one adultery.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r4.anchor: ما ظهر الخمر وما بطن الزنا قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r5.claim: Qatada takes the wording generally: indecencies publicly displayed and privately concealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r5.anchor: أنه عام في الفواحش وظاهرها علانيتها وباطنها سرها قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi says outward indecencies are bodily acts and hidden ones are beliefs of the heart, paralleling 7:33.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r6.anchor: ما ظهر أفعال الجوارح وما بطن اعتقاد القلوب ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r7.claim: The protected life is that of a Muslim or a person under treaty; killing is permitted only by authorization of religious law.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148/r7.anchor: والنفس التي حرم الله نفس مسلم أو معاهد والمراد بالحق إذن الشرع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r1.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says anyone wanting to read the Prophet's sealed written testament should recite the An'am verses beginning here through the closing command to be mindful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: من أراد أن يقرأ صحيفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التي عليها خاتمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the An'am passages here decisive verses and foundations of scripture, then recites this commandment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r2.anchor: قال: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: في (2) الأنعام آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r3.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reports that the Prophet took a pledge on three matters, reciting these prohibitions: the faithful receive reward, breaches may be punished in this life, and those deferred to the next rest with God, who may punish or forgive. Al-Hakim grades it authentic, though Bukhari and Muslim transmit only the shorter pledge; Ibn Kathir says Sufyan may preserve both reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r3.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أيكم يبايعني على ثلاث؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r4.claim: Muhammad is told to address polytheists who worship others, forbid God's provision, and kill children under Satan's prompting: come hear what God truly forbade by revelation, not conjecture.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p359/r4.anchor: وأما تفسيرها فيقول تعالى لنبيه ورسوله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: قل يا محمد -لهؤلاء المشركين الذين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r1.claim: The opening prohibition omits an understood phrase, 'and He commanded you'; the verse's conclusion and an Arabic poetic example support this ellipsis.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r1.anchor: وكأن في الكلام محذوفا دل عليه السياق، وتقديره: وأوصاكم (1) {ألا تشركوا به شيئا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r2.claim: Abu Dharr reports Gabriel's assurance that a member of the Prophet's community who dies without associating partners with God enters Paradise even if guilty of adultery, theft, or drinking wine; a variant has the Prophet add despite Abu Dharr's displeasure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r2.anchor: من حديث أبي ذر، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أتاني جبريل فبشرني أنه من مات لا يشرك بالله شيئا من أمتك، دخل الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r3.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r3.claim: In a sacred report to Abu Dharr, God promises forgiveness to one who invokes and hopes in Him, even with earthful sins, provided the person does not associate partners with Him; sincere later repentance is also forgiven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r3.anchor: عن أبي ذر [رضي الله عنه] (6) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يقول الله تعالى: يا ابن آدم، إنك ما دعوتني ورجوتني فإني أغفر لك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r4.claim: Qur'an 4:48 and 4:116 says God does not forgive shirk but may forgive lesser sins; Ibn Mas'ud's report likewise promises Paradise to one who dies without shirk, and many other texts support this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r4.anchor: قال الله تعالى (8) : {إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r5.claim: Reports from Ubadah and Abu al-Darda command believers not to associate partners with God even if burned, cut, or crucified; Ubadah also lists this as the first of seven counsels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p360/r5.anchor: وروى ابن مردويه من حديث عبادة وأبي الدرداء: "لا تشركوا بالله شيئا، وإن قطعتم أو صلبتم أو حرقتم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r1.claim: The command concerning parents means God commands people to treat them excellently, as reiterated in Isra'.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وبالوالدين إحسانا} أي: وأوصاكم وأمركم بالوالدين إحسانا، أي: أن تحسنوا إليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r2.speaker: reader
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r2.claim: Some readers use the variant 'wa-waṣṣā rabbuka' (your Lord commanded), supporting the construction of the preceding command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r2.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: "ووصى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r3.claim: Scripture often pairs obedience to God with kindness to parents; even when parents are polytheists, one should treat them well without obeying their call to shirk, as in Luqman and the Israelite covenant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r3.anchor: كما قال: {أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير * وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that the deeds most loved by God are prayer on time, filial kindness, then striving in God's cause; the Prophet might have named more had Ibn Mas'ud asked.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي العمل أحب إلى الله؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r5.claim: Weakly transmitted reports from Abu al-Darda and Ubadah say the Prophet advised obeying parents even if they ordered one to leave all worldly possessions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361/r5.anchor: بسنده عن أبي الدرداء، وعن عبادة بن الصامت، كل منهما يقول: أوصاني خليلي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أطع والديك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r1.claim: After commanding kindness to parents, God commands care for children; people killed daughters from shame and sometimes sons from fear of poverty, under satanic temptation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا يقتلون أولادهم كما سولت لهم الشياطين ذلك، فكانوا يئدون البنات خشية العار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet ranking associating partners with God as the greatest sin, followed by killing a child from fear of sharing food and then adultery with a neighbor's wife; he recited the parallel list in Furqan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p361#2/r2.anchor: قلت: يا رسول الله، أي الذنب أعظم؟ قال: "أن تجعل لله ندا وهو خلقك". قلت: ثم أي؟ قال: "أن تقتل ولدك خشية أن يطعم معك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Suddi gloss poverty as present destitution; by contrast, 17:31 forbids killing children for fear of future poverty and puts their provision first, while this verse addresses current poverty and puts parents first.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة، والسدي: هو الفقر، أي: ولا تقتلوهم من فقركم الحاصل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r2.claim: The ban on manifest and hidden indecencies parallels the comprehensive prohibition in A'raf and the earlier call to leave outward and inward sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r2.anchor: كقوله تعالى: {قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet saying no one is more jealous than God, and because of His jealousy He forbade both open and hidden indecencies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا أحد أغير من الله، من أجل ذلك حرم الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r4.claim: When Sa'd ibn Ubada threatened a man he found with his wife, the Prophet said he was more jealous than Sa'd and God more jealous than he; that divine jealousy is why indecencies are forbidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r4.anchor: فبلغ ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: "أتعجبون من غيرة سعد! فوالله لأنا أغير من سعد، والله أغير مني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r5.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra likewise says God is jealous and forbids indecencies; Ibn Mardawayh alone transmits it, though Ibn Kathir says this chain matches one used for another report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قيل: يا رسول الله، إنا (4) . نغار. قال: "والله إني لأغار، والله أغير مني، ومن غيرته نهى عن الفواحش"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.claim: The explicit ban on killing a protected soul reiterates a prohibition already included in the ban on manifest and hidden abominations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r1.anchor: وهذا مما نص تبارك وتعالى على النهي عنه تأكيدا، وإلا فهو داخل في النهي عن الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.claim: The Prophet limits lawful Muslim blood to three cases: a married adulterer, a life taken in retaliation, or one who abandons religion and the community; Ibn Kathir cites the report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.claim: A Muslim's blood is lawful only for a married adulterer to be stoned, an intentional killer to be killed, or an apostate who wages war against God and His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r3.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r4.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r4.claim: While besieged, Uthman invokes a Prophetic report listing apostasy, adultery after marriage, and killing as the only grounds for Muslim blood, asserts his innocence of all three, and is killed unjustly; al-Tirmidhi grades it ḥasan.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.claim: The Prophet warns that killing a treaty-protected non-Muslim bars the killer from even smelling Paradise, whose scent reaches forty years' distance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، رضي الله عنهما، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.claim: The Prophet warns that one who violates God’s and His Messenger’s covenant with a protected person will not smell Paradise, whose scent reaches seventy autumns away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p362#2/r6.anchor: فلا يرح رائحة الجنة، وإن ريحها ليوجد من مسيرة سبعين خريفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363/r1.claim: God's injunctions are given so people may understand and heed His commands and prohibitions.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363/r2.claim: The report is transmitted by Ibn Mājah and al-Tirmidhi, who grade it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363/r2.anchor: رواه ابن ماجه، والترمذي وقال: حسن صحيح

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r1.claim: God left people unforced for moral responsibility and testing, so they must follow evidence rather than caprice; imitation, habit, doubt, neglect of inquiry, and worldly motives lead to ruin.
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r1.anchor: والامتحان، وتدل على أن الواجب اتباع الدليل فقط، دون اتباع الهوى

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r2.claim: Taʿālaw means ‘come near’; the word comes from elevation, as if the caller speaks from a high place.
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r2.anchor: معنى تعال: أقبل وادن، وأصله: من العلو والارتفاع

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r3.claim: Taḥrīm fundamentally means preventing or forbidding; it is related to ḥajr and ḥaẓr and opposed to release or permission.
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r3.anchor: والتحريم: أصله المنع، ونظيره: الحجر والحظر

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r4.claim: Recitation is distinct from the recited original speech, just as a retelling differs from what is retold; it can mean reading or repeating a narration.
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r4.anchor: والتلاوة: القراءة، والتلاوة غير المتلو كما أن الحكاية غير المحكي

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r5.claim: Imlāq means poverty or having no provisions; the related words for flattery suggest a poor person striving to draw near for gain.
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r5.anchor: والإملاق: الإفلاس من المال والزاد، وهو الفقر

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r6.claim: Fawāḥish are deeds greatly foul, and waṣṣā and awṣā both mean enjoining or charging someone with an instruction.
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r6.anchor: والفواحش: جمع فاحشة، وهو: القبيح العظيم في القبح، ووصى وأوصى بمعنى.

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r7.claim: ما may be the object of ‘recite,’ meaning what was forbidden, or the object of ‘forbid,’ meaning ‘what thing did your Lord forbid?’
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r7.anchor: فيه وجهان: الأول: نصب ب (أتل) أي: أتل الذي حرم عليكم.

JISHUMI:v4p2461/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r8.claim: The initial alif of أتلو is omitted because the jussive particle's deletion rule found no added letter to remove.
JISHUMI:v4p2461/r8.anchor: قلنا: لأن الجازم لما كان عمله الحذف فلم يصادف زيادة عمل في النفس

JISHUMI:v4p2462/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2462/r1.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v4p2462/r1.claim: ألا تشركوا may be nominative, accusative under ‘enjoined,’ ‘recite,’ or ‘forbade,’ a substitute, an exhortation, or a free-standing prohibition; تشركوا may be subjunctive under أن or jussive under لا.
JISHUMI:v4p2462/r1.anchor: موضع (أن) فيه ثلاثة أقوال: الأول: الرفع على تقدير: ذلك ألا تشركوا به شيئا.

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r1.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r1.claim: The prohibition of shirk and command to avoid it are equivalent; forbidding shirk states the same rule as commanding that it not be done.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r1.anchor: لا فرق بين قوله: حرم ربكم عليكم، وبين قوله: أمر ألا تفعلوا

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r2.claim: Alternatively, the text pairs prohibitions with corresponding duties, details what is recited rather than what is forbidden, or uses an exhortation construction.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r2.anchor: فمما حرم فعله الشرك، وأوجب ألا تشركوا، وحرم العقوق، وأوجب الإحسان

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r3.claim: The verse prohibits worshipping or claiming divinity for anything alongside God and commands kindness to parents, whose care follows God's in nurturing people.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r3.anchor: يعني في العبادة وادعاء الإلهية وبالوالدين إحسانا يعني أمركم بالإحسان إلى الوالدين

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وابن جريج والضحاك
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r4.claim: ‘Do not kill your children from poverty’ addresses killing children, including burying daughters alive for fear of hardship; God provides for parents and children.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r4.anchor: قيل: من الفقر، عن ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وابن جريج والضحاك

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r5.claim: Indecencies can include all sins or adultery; the author favors a broad ban on major sins, publicly and privately. Reports distinguish outward and inward acts and what is visible or hidden.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r5.anchor: قيل: المعاصي والقبائح كلها، وقيل: الزنا، وقيل: يدخل الصغير والكبير

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والسدي
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r6.claim: The public/hidden distinction forbids secret adultery, which some people did not consider wrong; another report says it corrects a false assumption about private conduct.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r6.anchor: قيل: لأنهم كانوا لا يرون بالزنا سرا بأسا فنهى عن ذلك، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r7.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r7.claim: One gloss makes public indecency wine and hidden indecency adultery.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r7.anchor: وقيل: ما ظهر الخمر، وما بطن الزنا عن الضحاك

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r8.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r8.claim: Public and hidden indecencies may mean deeds visible to people and deeds concealed from them.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو ما ظهر للناس وما هو باطن عنهم، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r9.claim: The prohibition on killing a protected person is repeated despite being included among indecencies to emphasize its gravity; protected lives include believers and treaty partners.

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r10.claim: ‘Except by right’ allows killing for apostasy, adultery by a married person, unjust murder, rebellion against a just imam, highway robbery, or in self-defense.
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r10.anchor: وهو الردة والزنا إذا كان محصنا

JISHUMI:v4p2463/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2463/r11.claim: God commanded these matters so people would learn and comply, recognize His mercy, and use reason to identify their duties.

JISHUMI:v4p2465/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r1.claim: The exception to the prohibition on killing is general and needs specification; the Prophet explains it as apostasy after faith, adultery after chastity, and unjust killing.
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r1.anchor: الاستثناء مجملا كان المستثنى منه أيضا مجملا فيحتاج إلى بيان

JISHUMI:v4p2465/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r2.claim: These acts are human acts subject to reward and punishment, against the Compulsionists' account of created acts.
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r2.anchor: وتدل أن هذه الأشياء فعلهم؛ لذلك تعلق به الأمر والنهي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r1.claim: Taʿālaw began as an invitation spoken from a high place to those below, then broadened to a general invitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r1.anchor: من الخاص الذي صار عاما ، وأصله أن يقوله من كان في مكان عال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r2.claim: Mā ḥarrama is the object of recitation or an indirect question; anlā is explanatory and lā prohibitive.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r2.anchor: منصوب بفعل التلاوة ، أي أتل الذي حرمه ربكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r3.claim: Do not treat anlā as an accusative particle with ‘do not associate’ as an apposition; prohibitions coordinate with the ensuing imperatives.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r3.anchor: نواهي لانعطاف الأوامر عليها ، وهي قوله : { وبالوالدين إحسانا }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.claim: For the fatha reading of ‘and this is My path,’ supply a purpose lām: follow it because it is straight; the kasra reading gives the same cause, supported by 72:18.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.anchor: قلت : أجعل قوله : { وأن هاذا صراطي مستقيما } ( الأنعام : 153 ) علة للاتباع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.claim: The commands and prohibitions share the opening ruling; it prohibits their opposites, including mistreating parents, short measures, unjust speech, and breaking the covenant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.anchor: علم أن التحريم راجع إلى أضدادها ، وهي الإساءة إلى الوالدين ، وبخس الكيل والميزان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r6.claim: Min imlāq means because of poverty or fear of poverty, as in 17:31.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r6.anchor: من أجل فقر ومن خشيته ، كقوله تعالى : { خشية إملاق } ( الإسراء : 31 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r7.claim: ‘What is apparent and hidden’ parallels the outward and inward sin mentioned in 6:120.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r7.anchor: مثل قوله : { ظاهر الإثم وباطنه } ( الأنعام : 120 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r8.claim: Killing ‘except by right’ includes retaliation, execution for apostasy, and stoning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r1.claim: God commands the Prophet to invite people and recite what God forbids and permits, correcting pre-Islamic practice of forbidding lawful things and permitting unlawful ones.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r1.anchor: وهذا أمر من الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم , أن يدعو الناس إليه ليتلو عليهم ما حرمه الله عليهم , وما أحله لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r2.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r2.claim: Tilāwa and qirāʾa refer to the first recitation, while matluw and maqruʾ refer to later repetitions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r2.anchor: والفرق بين التلاوة والمتلو , والقراءة والمقروء أن التلاوة والقراءة للمرة الأولى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r3.claim: The distinction is instead that tilāwa and qirāʾa denote the spoken wording, while matluw and maqruʾ denote what is uttered.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r3.anchor: أن التلاوة والقراءة يتناول اللفظ , والمتلو والمقروء يتناول الملفوظ

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r4.claim: “Do not associate anything with Him” may prohibit worshipping a devil or idol alongside God, and may encompass both relevant forms of association.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r4.anchor: ألا تشركوا بعبادته عبادة غيره من شيطان أو وثن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r5.claim: Kindness to parents means fulfilling their rights, avoiding disobedience, and maintaining dutiful care.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r5.anchor: والإحسان تأدية حقوقهما ومجانبة عقوقهما والمحافظة على برهما

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r6.claim: People in pre-Islamic Arabia killed their children for fear of poverty; imlāq can mean insolvency, related to a bankrupt person's effort to ingratiate himself for delay.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r6.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا في الجاهلية يقتلون أولادهم خشية الإملاق . وفي الإملاق قولان : أحدهما : أنه الإفلاس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي والضحاك وابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r7.claim: Imlāq may simply mean poverty, close in meaning to insolvency despite a distinction between them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r7.anchor: أن الإملاق ومعناهما قريب وإن كان بينهما فرق

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r8.claim: God provides for both caretakers and children, since the Creator guarantees everyone's provision.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r8.anchor: لأن رزق العباد كلهم , من كفيل ومكفول , على خالقهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r9.claim: Avoiding both public and hidden indecencies applies generally to all indecencies.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r9.anchor: أن ذلك عام في جميع الفواحش سرها وعلانيتها , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r10.claim: The phrase may specifically refer to fornication: public prostitutes are overt, and clandestine lovers are hidden.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r10.anchor: ما ظهر منها : ذوات الحوانيت , وما بطن : ذوات الاستسرار

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r11.speaker: مجاهد وابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r11.claim: The overt indecencies are unlawful marriages and the hidden one is fornication.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r11.anchor: ما ظهر منها : نكاح المحرمات , وما بطن : الزنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r12.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r12.claim: Wine is an overt indecency and fornication a hidden one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r12.anchor: ما ظهر منها : الخمر , وما بطن منها : الزنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r13.claim: Another possible distinction is overt bodily acts versus hidden beliefs of the heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r13.anchor: ما ظهر منها أفعال الجوارح , وما بطن منها اعتقاد القلوب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r14.claim: The Prophet states that a Muslim's blood is inviolable except for apostasy after faith, adultery after marriage, or a life taken in retaliation for murder.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r14.anchor: لا يحل دم امرىء مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث : كفر بعد إيمان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r15.claim: The prohibition of killing except by right is God's binding command to His servants.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r15.anchor: يعني أن الله وصى عباده بذلك , ووصية الله واجبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r16.claim: “So that you may reason” may mean understand the prohibition or behave rationally by avoiding deeds that bring punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p184/r16.anchor: تعقلون تحريم ذلك عليكم وتعلمونه . والثاني : تعملون عمل من يعقل

MUQATIL:6:151-152/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:151-152/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:151-152/r1.claim: The prohibitions include shirk, honoring parents, killing daughters from fear of poverty, public or secret adultery, and killing protected life except by retaliation, stoning of a married adulterer, or apostasy; pre-Islamic camel taboos are not forbidden here.
MUQATIL:6:151-152/r1.anchor: يعني دفن البنات وهن أحياء، { من إملاق } ، يعني خشية الفقر،

MUQATIL:6:151-152/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:151-152/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:151-152/r2.claim: “Foul deeds” means adultery, public or secret; lawful execution is limited to retaliation, a married adulterer, or an apostate from Islam.
MUQATIL:6:151-152/r2.anchor: يعني بالقصاص والثيب الزاني بالرجم، والمرتد عن الإسلام،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r1.claim: The call addresses people who prohibited crops and livestock; تعالوا originally invited someone below from a higher place before becoming a general invitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r1.anchor: هو من الخاص الذى صار عام وأصله أن يقوله من كان فى مكان عال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r2.claim: The phrase ألا تشركوا explains what is recited, rather than supplying a prohibition particle.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r2.anchor: أى مفسرة لفعل التلاوة ولا للنهى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r3.claim: Kindness to parents appears among prohibitions because requiring kindness necessarily forbids neglecting it; the same applies to the following commands.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r3.anchor: ولما كان إيجاب الإحسان تحريما لترك الإحسان ذكر فى المحرمات وكذا حكم ما بعده

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r4.claim: Do not kill children from poverty or fear of poverty; God provides for parents and children because He sustains His servants.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r4.anchor: ﴿ ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق ﴾ من أجل فقر ومن خشيته كقوله خشية إملاق ﴿ نحن نرزقكم وإياهم ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r5.claim: Public indecencies concern conduct between people, private ones what is between a person and God; the public phrase apposes الفواحش.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r5.anchor: ﴿ ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها ﴾ ما بينك وبين الخلق ﴿ وما بطن ﴾ ما بينك وبين الله ما ظهر بدل من الفواحش

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r6.claim: A protected life may be taken only by right, such as retaliation, execution for apostasy, or stoning.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r7.claim: These detailed commands are what God charged people to preserve, so they may recognize their seriousness before Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352/r7.anchor: ﴿ ذلكم وصاكم به ﴾ أى المذكور مفصلا أمركم ربكم بحفظه

SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r1.claim: Mā in ‘recite what your Lord has forbidden’ is most likely a relative pronoun, object of ‘recite,’ with its resumptive pronoun omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r1.anchor: في " ما " هذه ثلاثة أوجه أظهرها: أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي والعائد محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r2.claim: Alternatively mā is a verbal noun: ‘recite your Lord’s prohibition’; the verbal noun stands for the prohibited thing because the act of prohibition itself cannot be recited.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون مصدرية أي: أتل تحريم ربكم، ونفس التحريم لا يتلى وإنما هو مصدر واقع موقع المفعول به

SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r3.claim: A third, weak option makes mā interrogative, asking ‘what did your Lord forbid?’; suspension of ‘recite’ is limited to verbs of thought and their analogues.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r3.anchor: أنها استفهامية في محل نصب بحرم بعدها

SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r4.claim: ‘Upon you’ may modify ḥarrama according to Basrans or atlu according to Kufans; this reflects their preference for the second or first verb in a competing-governance construction.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151/r4.anchor: أنه متعلق بحرم، وهذا اختيار البصريين.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r1.claim: Come means come forward and hear a certain, true recitation revealed by God, not conjecture or falsehood as the opponents alleged.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r1.anchor: أي تقدموا واقرءوا حقا يقينا كما أوحى إلي ربي، لا ظنا ولا كذبا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r2.speaker: ابن الشجري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r2.claim: Ibn al-Shajari explains the forms of ta'ala for singulars and groups; the word first meant rise and come forward, then broadened to include someone already standing or walking.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r2.anchor: وجعلوا التقدم ضربا من التعالي والارتفاع لأن المأمور بالتقدم في أصل وضع هذا الفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r3.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r3.claim: The Basran analysis attaches alaykum to the nearer verb harama, making ma the object of atlu; the Kufan analysis attaches it to the earlier atlu.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r3.anchor: فإن علقت «عليكم» ب «حرم» فهو الوجه لأنه الأقرب وهو اختيار البصريين

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r4.speaker: ابن الشجري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r4.claim: Ibn al-Shajari analyzes alla tushriku as an accusative after an implied repeated verb, or as an exhortation in which alaykum stands independently; al-Nahhas offers apposition to ma, while al-Farra takes la as prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r4.anchor: ألا تشركوا } في موضع نصب بتقدير فعل من لفظ الأول، أي أتل عليكم ألا تشركوا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r5.claim: The verse commands the Prophet to summon all people to hear God's prohibitions; later scholars must likewise teach people what is forbidden and lawful.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151/r5.anchor: هذه الآية أمر من الله تعالى لنبيه عليه السلام بأن يدعو جميع الخلق إلى سماع تلاوة ما حرم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r1.claim: The obligation to explain prohibitions is reinforced by the command that scripture be made clear to people rather than concealed.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r2.speaker: ربيع بن خيثم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak reports Rabi ibn Khuthaym asking a companion if he would like a sealed letter from the Prophet; he then reads this verse through the end of the three verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r2.anchor: قال ربيع بن خيثم لجليس له: أيسرك أن تؤتى بصحيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r3.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r3.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says this passage opens the Torah.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r3.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: هذه الآية مفتتح التوراة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are the decisive verses mentioned in Aal Imran, agreed upon by revealed laws and never abrogated; another view identifies them as the Ten Commandments given to Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هذه الآيات المحكمات التي ذكرها الله في سورة «آل عمران

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r5.claim: Ihsan to parents entails honoring, caring for, protecting, obeying, freeing them from bondage, and not exercising domination over them; grammatically ihsanan is an accusative verbal noun with an implied command.
