QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r5.anchor: الإحسان إلى الوالدين برهما وحفظهما وصيانتهما وامتثال أمرهما وإزالة الرق عنهما

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r6.claim: Imلاق means poverty: do not bury daughters or kill children out of fear of hardship, because God provides for parents and children; some also killed boys and girls from poverty.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r6.anchor: الإملاق الفقر: أي لا تئدوا من الموءودة بناتكم خشية العيلة، فإني رازقكم وإياهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r7.speaker: مؤرج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r7.claim: Mu'rij says imlaq means hunger in the language of Lakhm.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r7.anchor: وحكى النقاش عن مؤرج أنه قال: الإملاق الجوع بلغة لخم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r8.speaker: منذر بن سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r8.claim: Mundhir ibn Sa'id says imlaq means spending, citing the verb for spending away one's property and a saying attributed to Ali.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r8.anchor: وذكر منذر بن سعيد أن الإملاق الإنفاق

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r9.claim: The word malq can mean a flatterer who promises with his tongue what he does not hold in his heart, illustrating the root's range.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r9.anchor: ورجل ملق يعطي بلسانه ما ليس في قلبه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r10.claim: Some infer that coitus interruptus is forbidden by analogy to infanticide, since killing removes existing offspring while withdrawal prevents offspring at their origin; others say the Prophet's description of it as hidden infanticide signals dislike rather than prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r10.anchor: وقد يستدل بهذا من يمنع العزل لأن الوأد يرفع الموجود والنسل والعزل منع أصل النسل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r11.claim: The Prophet called coitus interruptus hidden infanticide, a report used to argue against it.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#2/r11.anchor: قوله عليه السلام في العزل: «ذلك الوأد الخفي»

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r1.speaker: جماعة من الصحابة وغيرهم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r1.claim: A group of Companions, Successors, and jurists permit withdrawal, citing the Prophet's statement that there is no blame in refraining because destiny determines conception; Hasan and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna understood the report as discouraging it.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r1.anchor: لا عليكم ألا تفعلوا فإنما هو القدر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers permissibility as the first interpretation because nothing can prevent a child if God wills its creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r2.anchor:
والتأويل الأول أولى لقوله عليه السلام:
" وإذا أراد الله خلق شيء لم يمنعه شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r3.speaker: مالك والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r3.claim: Malik and al-Shafi'i require a free wife’s permission for withdrawal, viewing ejaculation as part of her pleasure and her right to children; they see no such right for a concubine.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r3.anchor: لا يجوز العزل عن الحرة إلا بإذنها

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r4.claim: All indecencies are prohibited, whether outward acts or inwardly held disobedience; outward and inward together exhaust the categories, and the phrase is grammatically appositional to al-fawahish.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r4.anchor: فقوله: «ما ظهر» نهي عن جميع أنواع الفواحش وهي المعاصي. «وما بطن» ما عقد عليه القلب من المخالفة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.claim: The generic definite al-nafs parallels generic human statements qualified by exceptions; the verse forbids killing any protected life, Muslim or treaty-holder, except for a legally valid cause.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية نهي عن قتل النفس المحرمة، مؤمنة كانت أو معاهدة إلا بالحق

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r6.claim: The Prophet says that anyone who testifies to God's oneness is protected in life and property, except by a rightful legal claim, and is answerable to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r6.anchor: فمن قال لا إله إلا الله فقد عصم ماله ونفسه إلا بحقه وحسابهم على الله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r7.claim: Examples of a lawful cause include withholding zakat and abandoning prayer; Abu Bakr fought those who withheld zakat, and a Quranic verse orders release when people repent, pray, and give alms.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r7.anchor: وهذا الحق أمور: منها منع الزكاة وترك الصلاة وقد قاتل الصديق مانعي الزكاة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r1.claim: The lawful exceptions to the prohibition on killing include the cases named in 9:5, including a previously married adulterer, retaliation for murder, and apostasy with departure from the community.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r1.anchor: لا يحل دم امرىء مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r2.claim: The Prophet instructed that when allegiance is given to two caliphs, the later claimant should be killed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r2.anchor: إذا بويع لخليفتين فاقتلوا الآخر منهما

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet ordered killing both the active and passive partners in male same-sex intercourse; Qurtubi says fuller treatment will come in al-Aʿraf.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r3.anchor: من وجدتموه يعمل عمل قوم لوط فاقتلوا الفاعل والمفعول به

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r4.claim: The exception also covers the prescribed punishment for those who wage war against God and spread corruption on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r4.anchor: إنما جزآء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r5.claim: The legal treatment of armed conflict among believers is also relevant to the qualification that killing must be justified.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r6.claim: One who breaks Muslim unity, defies the community's imam, loots families and property, rebels against authority, and refuses its judgment is to be killed as a corrupter; this explains “except by right.”
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r6.anchor: من شق عصا المسلمين وخالف إمام جماعتهم وفرق كلمتهم وسعى في الأرض فسادا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r7.claim: The Prophet said believers have equal standing in blood, even the least of them can give protection, a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever, a protected non-Muslim is not killed while under protection, and people of different religions do not inherit one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r7.anchor: المؤمنون تتكافأ دماؤهم ويسعى بذمتهم أدناهم لا يقتل مسلم بكافر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r8.claim: Abu Bakra reports the Prophet warning that someone who unjustly kills a protected non-Muslim is barred from Paradise; one version says its scent can be found from seventy years away.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r8.anchor: من قتل معاهدا في غير كنهه حرم الله عليه الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r9.claim: A version in Abu Dawud says the killer of a protected person will not smell Paradise, whose scent reaches from seventy years away; Bukhari's version from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr says forty years.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r9.anchor: من قتل رجلا من أهل الذمة لم يجد ريح الجنة وإن ريحها ليوجد من مسيرة سبعين عاما

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r10.claim: “That” points to the prohibitions just listed; the attached address pronouns are vocative and have no grammatical case, while “enjoined” means a decisive, actionable command and its subject pronoun refers to God.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r11.claim: Matar al-Warraq transmits through Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar that ʿUthman addressed his companions, asking why they were killing him and saying he had heard the Prophet state the rule on lawful Muslim blood.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153/r11.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر أن عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r1.claim: In the continuation of the report, ʿUthman swears he neither committed adultery, killed anyone liable to retaliation, nor apostatized, and affirms his faith; he says these were the matters God enjoined so people might understand.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r1.anchor: فوالله ما زنيت في جاهلية ولا إسلام

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r1.claim: After refuting the unbelievers’ false claims about what God prohibited, the verse states the actual prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r1.anchor: أردفه تعالى ببيان الأشياء التي حرمها عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf says taʿāl is originally a call from someone higher to someone below, but it became a general invitation.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ( تعال ) من الخاص الذي صار عاما

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r3.claim: The object in mā ḥarrama rabbukum may be governed by atlu, meaning recite what He prohibited, or by ḥarrama, meaning recite the things He prohibited you.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r3.anchor: وفي ناصبه وجهان : الأول : أنه منصوب بقوله : { اتل } والتقدير : أتل الذي حرمه عليكم

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r4.claim: The apparent problem is that the list under what God prohibited includes avoiding shirk and doing good to parents, which are obligations rather than prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r4.anchor: لأن ترك الشرك والإحسان بالوالدين واجب ، لا محرم

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r5.claim: One answer understands taḥrīm as God’s clearly fixed and delineated prescription, removing the objection about obligatory acts in the list.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r5.anchor: المراد من التحريم أن يجعل له حريما معينا ، وذلك بأن بينه بيانا مضبوطا معينا

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r6.claim: A second answer changes the clause boundary: the sentence may end at recite what God prohibited, after which a new clause begins with you must not associate, or it may end after prohibited you and begin with ألا تشركوا as lialla.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r6.anchor: أن الكلام تم وانقطع عند قوله { أتل ما حرم ربكم } ثم ابتدأ فقال : { عليكم أن * لا * تشركوا }

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r7.claim: A third answer takes أن as explanatory, effectively saying: recite what God prohibited, namely, do not associate anything with Him.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r7.anchor: أن تكون ( أن ) / في قوله : { أن لا * تشركوا } مفسرة بمعنى : أي

RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r8.claim: The excerpt then raises an unresolved objection: because kindness to parents is coordinated with the explanatory prohibition of shirk, the same reading appears to make parental kindness forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v13p189#2/r8.anchor: فإن قيل : فقوله : { وبالوالدين إحسانا } معطوف على قوله : { أن لا * تشركوا به شيئا }

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r1.claim: Because God commands kindness to parents, harming them is forbidden as its converse.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r1.anchor: لما أوجب الإحسان إليهما ، فقد حرم الإساءة إليهما

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r2.claim: The prohibition of associating anything with God answers the four groups of polytheists already refuted: idol worshippers, star worshippers, worshippers of jinn, and those who assign God children.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r2.anchor: فلما بين بالدليل فساد قول هؤلاء الطوائف . قال ههنا : { ألا تشركوا به شيئا } .

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r3.claim: The idolaters are those who took idols as partners, as in Abraham's objection to his father and people.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r3.anchor: طائفة من المشركين يجعلون الأصنام شركاء لله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r4.claim: A second group worshipped celestial bodies; Abraham refuted them by saying he did not love those that set.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r4.anchor: والطائفة الثانية : من المشركين عبدة الكواكب ، وهم الذين حكى الله عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r5.claim: A third group made jinn partners with God and professed Yazdan and Ahriman.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r5.anchor: والطائفة الثالثة : الذين حكى الله تعالى عنهم : { أنهم * جعلوا لله شركاء * الجن } وهم القائلون بيزدان وأهرمن .

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r6.claim: A fourth group assigned God sons and daughters; the preceding arguments expose the error of all these groups.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r6.anchor: والطائفة الرابعة : الذين جعلوا لله بنين وبنات ، وأقام الدلائل على فساد أقوال هؤلاء الطوائف والفرق

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r7.claim: Kindness to parents follows God's beneficence because God is the true cause of human existence and parents its outward cause, providing care and protection in childhood.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r7.anchor: لأن أعظم أنواع النعم على الإنسان نعمة الله تعالى ، ويتلوها نعمة الوالدين ، لأن المؤثر الحقيقي

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r8.claim: The prohibition targets killing children from fear of poverty, especially the burying of infant girls from jealousy or, more commonly, fear of destitution.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r8.anchor: والمراد منه النهي عن الوأد ، إذ كانوا يدفنون البنات أحياء ، بعضهم للغيرة ، وبعضهم خوف الفقر

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r9.claim: Since God guarantees provision for parents and children, parents should preserve each life and rely on God for its sustenance.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r9.anchor: فكما وجب على الوالدين تبقية النفس والاتكال في رزقها على الله ، فكذلك القول في حال الولد

RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r10.speaker: شمر
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r10.claim: Shammar says amlaqa can be intransitive for becoming poor or transitive for time destroying what someone has; imlāq means ruin.
RAZI-FULL:v13p190/r10.anchor: قال شمر : أملق ، لازم ومتعد . يقال : أملق الرجل ، فهو مملق ، إذا افتقر

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the manifest and hidden indecencies as adultery committed openly and secretly.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كانوا يكرهون الزنا علانية ، ويفعلون ذلك سرا ، فنهاهم الله عن الزنا علانية وسرا

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r2.claim: The author rejects restricting the prohibition to adultery: the general wording and general rationale cover every manifest and hidden indecency.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r2.anchor: والأولى أن لا يخصص هذا النهي بنوع معين ، بل يجري على عمومه في جميع الفواحش ظاهرها وباطنها لأن اللفظ عام

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r3.claim: Avoiding sin publicly but not inwardly shows concern for people's blame rather than worship of God; fearing their blame more than God's punishment risks unbelief, while avoiding both forms reflects reverence for God.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r3.anchor: دل ذلك على أن احترازه عنها ليس لأجل عبودية الله وطاعته ، ولكن لأجل الخوف من مذمة الناس ، وذلك باطل

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r4.claim: Murder is included among indecencies but singled out to magnify its gravity and to permit an explicit exception for justified killing.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r4.anchor: إحداهما : أن الإفراد بالذكر يدل على التعظيم والتفخيم ، كقوله : { وملئكته * وجبريل وميكال } والثانية : أنه تعالى أراد أن يستثني منه

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r5.claim: A prophetic report says a Muslim's blood is lawful only for unbelief after faith, adultery after marriage, or killing a person without right.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r5.anchor: والحديث أيضا موافق له وهو قوله عليه السلام : ( لا يحل دم امرىء مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث كفر بعد إيمان

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r6.claim: The Qur'an supplies a fourth ground for killing: those who wage war against God and His Messenger and spread corruption may be killed or crucified.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r6.anchor: والقرآن دل على سبب رابع ، وهو قوله تعالى : { إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون فى الارض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا }

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r7.claim: The default rule is that killing a protected person is forbidden; permissibility requires separate evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r7.anchor: الأصل في قتل النفس هو الحرمة وحله لا يثبت إلا بدليل منفصل

RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r8.claim: Calling the commands God's bequest conveys tenderness and kindness, helping the addressee accept them; reason enables recognition of their religious and worldly benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v13p191/r8.anchor: لما في هذه اللفظة من اللطف والرأفة ، وكل ذلك ليكون المكلف أقرب إلى القبول

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r1.claim: He treats أن as explanatory, لا as prohibitive, and تشركوا as jussive; the jussive fits the following commands and parallels Hud 11:85.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r1.anchor: وهو اختيار الفراء قال: " ويجوز أن يكون مجزوما ب " لا " على النهي

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r2.claim: He likewise reads أن as explanatory and لا as prohibitive; he interprets the following commands under the prohibition as bans on their opposites.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r2.anchor: وهو اختيار الزمخشري أيضا فإنه قال: " وأن في " أن لا تشركوا " مفسرة و " لا " للنهي

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r3.claim: He objects that putting the commands under the prohibition and interpreting them as bans on their opposites is remote and obscure.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r3.anchor: كون هذه الأشياء اشتركت في الدخول تحت حكم التحريم، وكون التحريم راجعا إلى أضداد الأوامر بعيد جدا

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r4.claim: The author rejects the objection that the opposites interpretation is remote or obscure.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r4.anchor: ما استبعده ليس ببعيد وأين الإلغاز والتعمي من هذا الكلام حتى يرميه به

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r5.claim: One alternative is to coordinate the commands with تعالوا أتل, not with the preceding prohibitions; the speech then gives an invitation followed by commands.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أنها معطوفة لا على المناهي قبلها فيلزم انسحاب التحريم عليها

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r6.claim: His second alternative coordinates commands with prohibitions under explanatory أن, supplying an omitted clause, what He commanded you, inferred from what He prohibited.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#2/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي وداخلة تحت " أن " التفسيرية، ويصح ذلك على تقدير محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r1.claim: The cited Arabic line supports coordinating a command with a prohibition; such coordination is accepted, unlike coordination among clauses of different types.
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r1.anchor:
يقولون لا تهلك أسى وتجمل
وهذا لا نعلم فيه خلافا بخلاف الجمل المتباينة بالخبر

SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r2.claim: Another analysis makes أن subjunctive and its clause a substitute for ما حرم; لا must then be extra to preserve the meaning, as in the cited verses.
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن تكون " أن " ناصبة للفعل بعدها، وهي وما في حيزها في محل نصب بدلا من " ما حرم

SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r3.claim: A third analysis makes the subjunctive clause a substitute for an omitted relative pronoun, with the same status as the preceding analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r3.anchor: الثالث: أنها الناصبة أيضا وهي وما في حيزها بدل من العائد المحذوف إذ التقدير: ما حرمه

SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r4.claim: He rejects making لا extra because only associating partners is prohibited and later لا clearly has its ordinary prohibitive force.
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r4.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لانحصار عموم المحرم في الإشراك، إذ ما بعده من الأمر ليس داخلا في المحرم

SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r5.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r5.claim: Makkī also makes the clause a substitute for ما حرم but does not mention that this requires treating لا as extra.
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r5.anchor: ولما ذكر مكي كونها بدلا من " ما حرم " لم ينبه على زيادة " لا " ولا بد منه

SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r6.claim: He rejects the substitute analysis: the commands would coordinate with prohibitions, requiring the commands to be understood as prohibitions of opposites.
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r6.anchor: وقد منع الزمخشري أن تكون بدلا من " ما حرم " فقال: " فإن قلت: هلا قلت هي التي تنصب الفعل

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r1.claim: One analysis makes أن and its clause an accusative exhortation governed by عليكم, with the preceding clause ending at ربكم; the author considers it weak.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r1.anchor: أن تكون " أن " الناصبة وما في حيزها منصوبة على الإغراء ب " عليكم " ، ويكون الكلام الأول قد تم عند قوله " ربكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r2.claim: The exhortative analysis is weak because it disrupts the apparent construction and is not the reading that first occurs to the listener.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r2.anchor: وهذا وإن كان ذكره جماعة كما نقله ابن الأنباري ضعيف لتفكك التركيب عن ظاهره

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r3.claim: He makes the clause genitive or accusative after an omitted causal lām: the recitation tells what God prohibited so that people do not associate partners.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r3.anchor: التقدير: أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم لئلا تشركوا، وهذا منقول عن أبي إسحاق

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r4.claim: Some object that the causal analysis poorly explains the coordinated commands semantically and the prohibitions syntactically.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r4.anchor: استبعده من حيث إن ما بعده أمر معطوف بالواو ومناه معطوفة بالواو أيضا فلا يناسب أن يكون تبيينا

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r5.claim: Another analysis supplies أوصيكم as the governing verb; the following command about parents is understood with the same verb.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r5.anchor: أن تكون هي وما بعدها في محل نصب بإضمار فعل تقديره: أوصيكم أن لا تشركوا؛ لأن قوله " وبالوالدين إحسانا

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r6.claim: As a nominative predicate of an omitted subject, المتلو أن لا تشركوا is better than المحرم أن لا تشركوا because it does not require an extra لا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r6.anchor: إلا أن التقدير بنحو المتلو أحسن؛ لأنه لا يحوج إلى زيادة " لا

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r7.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r7.claim: He allows أن and its clause to be nominative after the preceding preposition, with the sense of عليكم عدم الإشراك and a pause at ربكم.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r7.anchor: وهذا مذهب لأبي بكر بن الأنباري فإنه قال: " ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع ب " على " كما تقول: عليكم الصيام والحج

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r8.claim: He replies that the commands need not all coordinate with لا تشركوا; بالوالدين إحسانا can instead coordinate with تعالوا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#3/r8.anchor: فقال: " لا يتعين أن تكون جميع الأوامر معطوفة على ما دخل عليه " لا " لأنا بينا جواز عطف

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r1.claim: The ninth analysis makes the clause nominative as the subject governed by the preceding preposition: عليكم عدم الإشراك.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r1.anchor: التاسع: أن يكون في موضع رفع بالفاعلية بالجار قبلها، وهو ظاهر قول ابن الأنباري المتقدم

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r2.claim: Across the analyses, أن لا تشركوا has one genitive, three nominative, and six accusative parses, ten in total.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r2.anchor: وقد تحصلت في محل " أن لا تشركوا " على ثلاثة أوجه، الرفع والنصب والجر، فالجر من وجه واحد

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r3.claim: شيئا can be the direct object or a cognate noun meaning an act of association.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r3.anchor: و " شيئا " فيه وجهان أحدهما: أنه مفعول به. والثاني: أنه مصدر أي إشراكا

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r4.anchor: والإملاق: الفقر في قول ابن عباس. وقيل: الجوع بلغة لخم

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r5.speaker: مؤرج
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r5.claim: He reports that إملاق means hunger in the language of Lakhm.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r5.anchor: وقيل: الجوع بلغة لخم، نقله مؤرج. وقيل: الإسراف

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r6.speaker: محمد بن نعيم الترمذي
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r6.claim: He interprets إملاق as extravagance, deriving it from أملق for overspending.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r6.anchor: وقيل: الإسراف، أملق أي: أسرف في نفقته، قاله محمد بن نعيم الترمذي

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r7.speaker: المنذر بن سعيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r7.claim: He explains إملاق as spending: أملق ماله means he spent his wealth.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r7.anchor: وقيل الإنفاق، أملق ماله أي أنفقه قاله المنذر ابن سعيد

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r8.speaker: شمر
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r8.claim: He gives فساد as another sense and says أملق can be intransitive for becoming poor or transitive for ruining what one has.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r8.anchor: والإملاق: الإفساد أيضا قاله شمر، قال: " وأملق يكون قاصرا ومتعديا، أملق الرجل: إذا افتقر

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r9.speaker: النضر بن شميل
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r9.claim: He cites Aws ibn Hajar's line to show أملق can mean that troubles take one's wealth away.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r9.anchor:
وأنشد النضر بن شميل على ذلك قول أوس بن حجر:
2119 ولما رأيت العدم قيد نائلي

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r10.claim: The order of رزقكُم وإياهم differs meaningfully: this verse reassures impoverished parents first, while 17:31 reassures solvent parents afraid of future poverty by naming children first.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#4/r10.anchor: وأحسن منه أن يقال: الظاهر من قوله " من إملاق " حصول الإملاق للوالد لا توقعه وخشيته

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r1.claim: ما ظهر منها وما بطن is an accusative inclusive substitute for الفواحش; من can also mark a partitive relation, and the second منها is omitted by ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r1.anchor: في محل نصب بدلا من الفواحش بدل اشتمال أي: لا تقربوا ظاهرها وباطنها

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r2.claim: إلا بالحق is either a circumstantial qualifier of the killer or an adjective of an omitted act of killing; lawful cases include retaliation, apostasy, or adultery under its conditions.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r2.anchor: إلا بالحق } في محل نصب على الحال من فاعل " تقتلوا " أي: لا تقتلوها

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r3.claim: Homicide is singled out after the general ban on atrocities to stress its gravity and because the exception by right would not work without naming it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#5/r3.anchor: هذا شبيه بما هو من ذكر الخاص بعد العام اعتناء بشأنه؛ لأن الفواحش يندرج فيها قتل النفس

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r1.claim: ذلكم is either a subject with the following verbal clause as predicate or an accusative object of an implied verb through الاشتغال.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r1.anchor: في محله قولان أحدهما: أنه مبتدأ، والخبر الجملة الفعلية بعده. والثاني: أنه في محل نصب بفعل مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r2.claim: The ending لعلكم تعقلون fits because reason is the basis of legal responsibility and these instructions.
SAMIN-DURR:6:151#6/r2.anchor: وناسب قوله هنا " لعلكم تعقلون " لأن العقل مناط التكليف والوصية بهذه الأشياء المذكورة

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r3.claim: The ban on associating partners with God covers every form of shirk, including worship of idols, celestial bodies, and jinn mentioned in this surah.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r3.anchor: the admonition against shirk here refers to all its forms

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r4.claim: The paired commands to worship God alone and honor parents recur elsewhere, linking proper worship with filial reverence and care.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r4.anchor: it indicates the importance of filial piety and suggests a relationship between proper worship of God and reverence and care for parents

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r5.claim: Human beings owe parents greatly because of their extensive care when the children were young, so parental duty follows worship of God.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r5.anchor: human beings are most indebted to their parents, given the extensive and solicitous care they were provided when they were young

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r6.claim: The warning against killing children for fear of poverty directs parents to trust God to provide for them and their children.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r6.anchor: indicating that they should rely upon God to provide for the needs of themselves and their children

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r7.claim: Killing a protected person is forbidden except as a warranted capital punishment, such as for murder or waging war against God and His Messenger.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r7.anchor: when it is warranted as a punishment for capital transgression, such as for murder or“waging war against God and His Messenger”

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r8.claim: Outward and inward indecencies mean public and private forms of wrongdoing.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r8.anchor: which often connotes specifically sexual transgression (see 4:15c; 4:22c), but which here more likely refers

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r9.claim: Although fawāḥish often means sexual transgression, here it more likely means serious sins and moral transgressions generally.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r9.anchor: but which here more likely refers to serious sins and moral transgressions of all sorts

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r10.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r10.claim: Avoiding sin in both public and private demonstrates true piety; private sin after public restraint shows fear of blame rather than obedience to God.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r10.anchor: if one were to avoid sin publicly, but commit it privately, it would indicate that one’s motivation was simply to avoid public blame and not to obey God (R)

ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r1.claim: ما may be the object of أتل, ‘recite what your Lord forbade,’ or the object of حرم, since recitation is like saying: ‘What has your Lord forbidden?’; the recitation may then be the prohibition of carrion and spilled blood.
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r1.anchor:
ف " ما " في موصع نصب إن شئت ب (أتل).
والمعنى تعالوا أتل الذي حرم ربكم عليكم،

ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r2.claim: ألا تشركوا may have an omitted lām of purpose: the recitation explains what is forbidden so they will not associate partners, since rejecting God’s lawful permissions treats another authority as equal to Him.
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r2.anchor: ويكون (ألا تشركوا) منصوبة بمعنى طرح اللام أي: أبين لكم الحرام لئلا تشركوا به شيئا،

ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, ألا تشركوا is governed by the sense ‘I recite to you the prohibition of associating partners with Him.’
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r3.anchor:
ويجوز أن يكون (ألا تشركوا) محمولا على المعنى، فيكون:
" أتل عليكم ألا تشركوا به شيئا "

ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r4.claim: A further parse carries ألا تشركوا on ‘I enjoin you,’ matching the following command to treat parents well as something enjoined.
ZAJJAJ:v2p303#2/r4.anchor:
وجائز أن يكون على معنى أوصيكم (ألا تشركوا به شيئا)
لأن قوله: (وبالوالدين إحسانا) محمول على معنى أوصيكم بالوالدين إحسانا.

ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r1.claim: من إملاق means because of poverty, or fear of poverty.
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r1.anchor: أي لا تقتلوا أولادكم من فقر، أي من خوف فقر.

ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r2.claim: ما ظهر منها وما بطن is an accusative apposition to الفواحش; tafsir calls hidden indecency adultery and public indecency taking suspicious lovers.
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r2.anchor:
بدل من الفواحش في موضع نصب.
المعنى لا تقربوا ما ظهر من الفواحش وما بطن،

ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r3.claim: The broader apparent sense includes associating partners, killing children, and declaring lawful things forbidden: all are indecencies, whether public or concealed.
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r3.anchor: وظاهر الكلام أن الذي جرى من الشرك بالله عز وجل وقتل الأولاد وجميع ما حرموه مما أحل الله عز وجل فواحش

ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r4.claim: ذلكم وصاكم به confirms that the earlier clauses mean ‘I enjoin you not to associate anything with God and to treat parents well.’
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r4.anchor:
وقوله: (ذلكم وصاكم به).
يدل على أن معنى (ألا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا).

TABATABAI:6:151-153/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r4.claim: One proposed derivation takes ta'al, come up, from elevation, as though the addressee were summoned from a higher place even when that is not literally so.
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r4.anchor: قيل تعال مشتق من العلو وهو أمر بتقدير أن الأمر في مكان عال

TABATABAI:6:151-153/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r5.claim: Tilawa is close in meaning to recitation or reading.

TABATABAI:6:151-153/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r6.claim: Some parse عليكم as an imperative noun meaning take, governing the prohibition; Tabataba'i rejects this because it conflicts with the reading suggested by the context.
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r6.anchor: وربما قيل إن { عليكم } اسم فعل بمعنى خذوا وقوله { أن لا تشركوا } معموله

TABATABAI:6:151-153/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r7.claim: Because the passage invites recitation, it reproduces revelation's own mixture of prohibitions and positive commands rather than recasting every item in one grammatical form.
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r7.anchor: وضع في الكلام عين ما جاء به الوحي في مورد المحرمات من النهي في بعضها

TABATABAI:6:151-153/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r8.claim: Shirk is listed first because it is the greatest injustice and, according to the cited verse, is not forgiven; every sin ultimately tends toward it while goodness tends toward monotheism.
TABATABAI:6:151-153/r8.anchor: وقد قدم الشرك على سائر المحرمات لأنه الظلم العظيم الذي لا مطمع في المغفرة

TABATABAI:6:151/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151/r1.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly places kindness to parents after affirming God's oneness, as in the command following exclusive worship and Luqman's warning against shirk.
TABATABAI:6:151/r1.anchor: عد في مواضع من القرآن الكريم إحسان الوالدين تاليا للتوحيد ونفي الشرك

TABATABAI:6:151/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:6:151/r2.claim: Al-Majma' paraphrases the command as God having enjoined kindness to parents; Tabataba'i notes that the word for forbidding also carries the sense of commanding avoidance.
TABATABAI:6:151/r2.anchor: وفي المجمع أي وأوصى بالوالدين إحسانا

TABATABAI:6:151/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151/r3.claim: Filial disobedience is among the greatest sins, perhaps the greatest after shirk, because human society depends on familial mercy and the reciprocal care of parents and children.
TABATABAI:6:151/r3.anchor: يدل ذلك على أن عقوق الوالدين من أعظم الذنوب أو هو أعظمها بعد الشرك بالله العظيم

TABATABAI:6:151/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151/r4.claim: Parents are naturally prompted to care for young children, while children are especially needed when parents age; widespread neglect would weaken procreation, family formation, kinship, and social solidarity.
TABATABAI:6:151/r4.anchor: جفاء الأولاد للوالدين وعقوقهم لهما يوم حاجتهما إليهم

TABATABAI:6:151/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151/r5.claim: Imlaq means poverty or depletion of money and provisions; in pre-Islamic Arabia, drought and fear of destitution led some fathers to kill children to avoid seeing them suffer hunger and humiliation.

TABATABAI:6:151/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151/r6.claim: The stated reason against killing children is that God provides for both parents and offspring, so fear of being unable to feed them is misplaced.
TABATABAI:6:151/r6.anchor: إنما تقتلونهم مخافه أن لا تقدروا على القيام بأمر رزقهم

TABATABAI:6:151/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151/r7.claim: Fawahish are plural of fahisha, ugly and reprehensible acts; the Qur'an includes adultery, sodomy, and slander of chaste women, while manifest and hidden refer to public and secret sexual relations.
TABATABAI:6:151/r7.anchor: الفواحش جمع فاحشة وهي الأمر الشنيع المستقبح

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r1.claim: Permitting indecency erases its stigma and encourages its spread because desire resists deprivation; this breaks lineage and family life, while permissive killing destroys public security and society's structure.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r1.anchor: وفي استباحة الفاحشة إبطال فحشها وشناعتها

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r2.claim: The protected life is either one whose killing God has forbidden or a person protected by revealed sanctity from loss of life or rights.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r2.anchor: أي حرم الله قتلها أو حرمها بالحرمة المشرعة لها التي تقيها وتحميها من الضيعة في دم أو حق

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r3.claim: Some explain the repeated murder prohibition as emphasizing its gravity even though it falls under indecency, as the separate ban on killing children receives special attention.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r3.anchor: قيل إنه تعالى أعاد ذكر القتل وإن كان داخلا في الفواحش تفخيما لشأنه

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r4.claim: The special mention of infanticide addresses Arabs who thought poverty excused killing offspring and believed parental status gave them ownership over children.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r4.anchor: وقد كانت العرب يفعل ذلك بزعمهم أن خشية الإملاق تبيح للوالد أن يقتل أولادة

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r5.claim: Killing a protected person is allowed only through a legally valid right, namely retaliation or a prescribed legal penalty.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r5.anchor: قتلها بالحق وهو القتل بالقود والحد الشرعي

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r6.claim: The first five prohibitions conclude with a call to reason; Tabataba'i postpones the explanation of this ending until his discussion of the three verse endings together.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r6.anchor: ثم أكد تحريم المذكورات في الآية بقوله { ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تعقلون }

TABATABAI:6:151-157/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r1.claim: The first verse's bans on shirk, filial neglect, infanticide, indecency, and unlawful murder are apparent to sound human reason once passion and dark emotion no longer obscure them, hence its call to reason.
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r1.anchor: مما تدرك الفطرة الإنسانية حرمتها في بادئ نظرها

TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r4.speaker: علي بن الحسين
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r4.claim: Ali b. al-Husayn glosses manifest indecencies as marrying one's father's wife and hidden indecencies as adultery; Tabataba'i says these are examples, not exhaustive definitions.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r4.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن قال ما ظهر

TABRISI:6:151/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151/r1.claim: Taʿālaw is an invitation upward even when speaker and hearer are on level ground; tilāwa is recitation distinct from the original recited speech, as narration differs from what it narrates. Imlāq means poverty; fawāḥish are gravely indecent acts.
TABRISI:6:151/r1.anchor: تعالوا مشتق من العلو على تقدير أن الداعي في المكان العالي وإن كان في مستو من الأرض

TABRISI:6:151/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151/r2.claim: The object of “recite what your Lord forbade” may be a relative clause, the object of forbidding, or an explanatory quotation of what He forbade; “that you associate nothing” can be parsed as an omitted purpose or as an injunction, following al-Zajjāj.
TABRISI:6:151/r2.anchor: ما حرم ربكم في موضع نصب بقوله أتل المعنى أتل الذي حرمه ربكم عليكم

TABRISI:6:151/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:151/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows “that you associate nothing” to depend on “I recite to you,” and takes “kindness to parents” as an understood “I enjoin you.”
TABRISI:6:151/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على معنى أوصيكم أن لا تشركوا به شيئا لأن قوله وبالوالدين إحسانا

TABRISI:6:151/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151/r4.claim: The verb “associate” may be subjunctive with an as-clause and negative lā, or jussive as a prohibition; in the former parse the later “do not kill” shifts from statement to prohibition, as in 6:14.
TABRISI:6:151/r4.anchor: وتشركوا يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بأن ويكون لا للنفي ويجوز أن يكون مجزوما بلا على النهي

TABRISI:6:151/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151/r5.speaker: البصير الأصفهاني
TABRISI:6:151/r5.claim: Al-Baṣīr al-Aṣfahānī proposes pausing after “upon you,” then beginning “that you associate not”; another possibility treats mā as interrogative and pauses after “your Lord.”
TABRISI:6:151/r5.anchor: وقال جامع العلوم البصير الأصفهاني يجوز أن تقف على عليكم ثم تبتدىء بأن لا تشركوا

TABRISI:6:151/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151/r6.claim: The list of prohibitions follows the account of the polytheists’ invented bans; the Prophet is told to invite them and begin with the prohibition of associating partners with God.
TABRISI:6:151/r6.anchor: لما حكى سبحانه عنهم تحريم ما حرموه عقبه بذكر المحرمات

TABRISI:6:151/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151/r7.claim: “Do not associate anything with Him” and “He forbids that you associate” express the same prohibition, since a command to refrain entails a ban.
TABRISI:6:151/r7.anchor: ولا فرق بين أن تقول لا تشركوا به شيئا وبين أن تقول حرم ربكم عليكم أن تشركوا به شيئا

TABRISI:6:151#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151#2/r1.claim: A further parsing ends the first clause at “your Lord forbade,” then treats “upon you, that you associate nothing” as an obligation, like the construction in 5:105.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r1.anchor: وقد قيل أيضا إن الكلام قد تم

TABRISI:6:151#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151#2/r2.claim: Kindness to parents is enjoined after worship of God because parents’ blessings follow God’s blessings in rank.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r2.anchor: ولما كانت نعم الوالدين تالية نعم الله سبحانه في الرتبة أمر بالإحسان إليهما

TABRISI:6:151#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:151#2/r3.claim: The ban on killing children from poverty addresses fear of destitution; God provides for both parents and children, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and others.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r3.anchor: أي خوفا من الفقر عن ابن عباس وغيره

TABRISI:6:151#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:6:151#2/r4.claim: “Do not approach indecencies, open or hidden” covers all sins and wrongs, whether outward or concealed, according to al-Ḥasan.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r4.anchor: أي المعاصي والقبائح كلها { ما ظهر منها وما بطن } أي ظاهرها وباطنها عن الحسن

TABRISI:6:151#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:151#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Suddī say people tolerated secret adultery while forbidding it publicly, so both are prohibited; Abū Jaʿfar identifies the apparent act as zina and the hidden one as an illicit intimate relationship.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: إنهم كانوا لا يرون بالزنا في السر بأسا ويمنعون منه علانية فنهى الله سبحانه عنه في الحالتين عن ابن عباس والضحاك والسدى

TABRISI:6:151#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s alternative takes the apparent as bodily acts and hidden as acts of the heart; the author says this is the broadest and most beneficial interpretation.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن ما ظهر أفعال الجوارح وما بطن أفعال القلوب فالمراد ترك المعاصي كلها وهذا أعم فائدة

TABRISI:6:151#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151#2/r7.claim: Homicide is repeated despite falling under indecencies to emphasize its gravity. The protected life is that of a Muslim or treaty-holder, not a combatant; lawful causes of execution are retaliation, adultery after chastity, and apostasy.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r7.anchor: أعاد ذكر القتل وإن كان داخلا في الفواحش تفخيما لشأنه وتعظيما لأمره

TABRISI:6:151#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151#2/r8.claim: The closing reminder means that God commanded these matters so people would understand, distinguish what He permits from what He forbids, and obey; “He enjoined” is understood in the opening list.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r8.anchor: خطاب لجميع الخلق أي ما ذكر في هذه الآية

TABRISI:6:151#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:151#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:151#2/r9.claim: The verse supports the theological principle that obligation includes refraining from an act, and that one deserves reward or punishment for refraining; this is the author’s school’s position.
TABRISI:6:151#2/r9.anchor: دلالة على أن التكليف قد يتعلق بأن لا يفعل كما يتعلق بالفعل

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls these rulings clear, un-abrogated prohibitions in all scriptures and universal commands for humanity: those who act on them enter Paradise and those who abandon them enter Hell.
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.speaker: كعب الأحبار
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār swears that these commands are the Torah’s first instruction, beginning with “Say: come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden.”
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذا لأول شيء في التوراة

THALABI:v4p202/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p202/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p202/r1.claim: ‘Come, I will recite’ means Muhammad is to proclaim with certainty what God truly forbade, as revelation and command, not speculation or denial.
THALABI:v4p202/r1.anchor: ثم قال قل يا محمد تعالوا أتل أقرأ ما حرم ربكم عليكم حقا يقينا

THALABI:v4p202/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p202/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p202/r2.claim: Grammarians differ on the case and construction of ألا تشركوا: it can complete حرم with an extra لا, or mean ‘that you do not associate’, or depend on أوحى.
THALABI:v4p202/r2.anchor: اختلفوا في محل أن فقال بعضهم: [محله] نصب، ثم اختلفوا في وجه انتصابه

THALABI:v4p202/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p202/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p202/r3.claim: Other analyses make ألا تشركوا an apposition to what God forbade, or place a break after حرم ربكم and read عليكم أن لا تشركوا.
THALABI:v4p202/r3.anchor: وقيل: أوحى ألا تشركوا، وقيل: [ما] بدل [من] ما حرم

THALABI:v4p202/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p202/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p202/r4.claim: The passage also discusses whether later prohibitions coordinate in the accusative or take a jussive construction, citing a command followed by a prohibition and poetry as grammatical evidence.
THALABI:v4p202/r4.anchor: ولا تكونن من المشركين عطف بالنهي على الخبر قال الشاعر: حج وأوصي بسليمي

THALABI:v4p202/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p202/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p202/r5.claim: The prohibition on killing children addresses burying daughters for fear of poverty: God provides for the parents and their children; إملَاق means poverty or depleted provisions.

THALABI:v4p203/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p203/r1.claim: Apparent indecencies are public acts and hidden ones are private acts; pre-Islamic people condemned public adultery but tolerated it in secret, so both are forbidden.
THALABI:v4p203/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: كانوا في الجاهلية يستقبحون الزنا في العلانية ولا يرون به بأسا في السر

THALABI:v4p203/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r2.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v4p203/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the apparent indecency as wine; the excerpt’s gloss of the hidden one is truncated.
THALABI:v4p203/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ما ظهر الخمر وما بطن

THALABI:v4p203/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p203/r3.claim: The protected life is that of a believer or treaty-holder; lawful exceptions are apostasy, retaliation for murder, and stoning for adultery after marriage.
THALABI:v4p203/r3.anchor: يعني بما أباح قبلها وهي الارتداد والقصاص والرجم

THALABI:v4p203/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r4.speaker: عثمان
THALABI:v4p203/r4.claim: Uthman cites the Prophet’s rule that Muslim blood is lawful only for a married adulterer, an intentional killer, or an apostate; he swears he committed none of these.
THALABI:v4p203/r4.anchor: وروى مطر الوراق عن نافع بن عمر عن عثمان رضي الله عنه أشرف على أصحابه وقال

THALABI:v4p204/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r7.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v4p204/r7.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says the command beginning ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord forbade’ was the first thing in the Torah.
THALABI:v4p204/r7.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذا لأول شيء في التوراة

THALABI:v4p204/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r8.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
THALABI:v4p204/r8.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khaytham recited these commands from a sealed sheet associated with Muhammad to his companions.
THALABI:v4p204/r8.anchor: وقال الربيع بن خيثم لأصحابه: ألا أقرأ عليكم صحيفة عليها خاتم محمد

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n146/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n146/r1.speaker: commentators
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n146/r1.claim: All commentators consider the bracketed command to do good to parents implied: it appears among prohibitions, although the Qur’an repeatedly enjoins filial goodness.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n146/r1.anchor: In the consensus of all the commentators, the phrase interpolated by me between brackets

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n147/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n147/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n147/r1.claim: The prohibition on killing children may refer to abortions motivated by economic concerns.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n147/r1.anchor: This may possibly refer to abortions dictated by economic considerations

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r1.claim: The injunction warns against using brute force to pursue private interests.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r1.anchor: not resort to brute force whenever your private interests are involved

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r2.claim: Killing in pursuit of justice includes legal punishment, defensive war, and legitimate individual self-defence.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n148/r2.anchor: the execution of a legal punishment or to killing in a just - that is, defensive-war

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r1.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r1.claim: Mā is accusative as the object of atlu: recite what your Lord has forbidden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r1.anchor: موضع (ما) نصب ب (أتل)، أي: اتل الذي حرمه ربكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r2.claim: An lā tushrikū can be accusative after an omitted lām, explaining what is forbidden; inventing religious prohibitions makes their inventors partners with God in authority.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r2.anchor: لأنهم إذا حرموا ما أحل الله عز وجل فقد جعلوا غير الله في القبول منه بمنزلة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is construed by meaning as “I recite to you the prohibition of shirk” or “I enjoin you not to associate,” parallel to the command to show kindness to parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r3.anchor: قال: ويجوز أن يكون {ألا تشركوا به}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r4.speaker: أبو بكر؛ الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r4.claim: Another analysis makes an accusative after ʿalaykum as exhortation, or nominative like “upon you is fasting”; al-Farrāʾ allows tushrikū to be subjunctive after an or jussive after lā, preferring jussive for the following commands, which may mix moods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p522/r4.anchor: والجزم في هذه الآية أحب إلي لقوله: {وأوفوا الكيل والميزان}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r1.claim: The command to show kindness to parents has an understood verb: “and that you do kindness,” coordinated with “that you not associate.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r1.anchor: التقدير: أن لا تشركوا به شيئا وأن تفعلوا {وبالوالدين إحسانا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r2.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r2.claim: Killing children from imlāq means fear of poverty; the parallel wording in 17:31 explicitly says fear of poverty and refers to burying daughters alive, from jealousy or want, while promising provision.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r3.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r3.claim: Amlaq can be intransitive for becoming poor and transitive for destroying what one owns; imlāq can mean ruin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r3.anchor: أملق الرجل فهو مملق إذا افتقر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r4.speaker: ابن شميل؛ أوس بن حجر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p524/r4.claim: A line by Aws ibn Ḥajar uses amlaqa for calamities consuming a person’s property.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r1.claim: People who avoided public adultery still committed it secretly; the prohibition covers both hidden and open fornication.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r1.anchor: كانوا يكرهون أن يزنوا علانية فيفعلون ذلك سرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r2.claim: Killing a protected soul “except by right” means legal retaliation, qiṣāṣ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r3.claim: The phrase “that is what He enjoins” shows that the preceding commands mean “He enjoins you not to associate partners and to show kindness to parents.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r3.anchor: هذا يدل على أن معنى {ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا} محمول

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r3.claim: God’s prohibitions begin with avoiding association and treating parents well, and forbid killing children from poverty, open or secret adultery, and killing except in lawful retaliation.

ELMALILI:6:151/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r1.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:6:151/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas calls these decisive rulings, never abrogated in any scripture and forbidden to all humanity.
ELMALILI:6:151/r1.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretleri demiştir ki: Bu âyetler o âyât-ı muhkemâttır ki kitapların hiçbirinde neshedilmemiştir

ELMALILI:6:151/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r2.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:6:151/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever follows these rulings enters Paradise and whoever does not enters Hell.
ELMALILI:6:151/r2.anchor: Bunlarla amel eden cennete girer, etmeyen cehenneme

ELMALILI:6:151/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r3.speaker: Ka‘bu’l-Ahbâr
ELMALILI:6:151/r3.claim: Ka‘b al-Ahbar says these verses form the beginning of the Torah.
ELMALILI:6:151/r3.anchor: Ka‘bu’l- Ahbâr da demiştir ki bu âyetler Tevrat’ın başlangıcıdır

ELMALILI:6:151/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r4.claim: The author says all revealed laws converge on these rulings, also described as the ten commandments revealed to Moses.
ELMALILI:6:151/r4.anchor: bütün şerâyi‘-i halk bunlar üzerinde ictimâ‘etmiş, bunların Mûsâ aleyhisselâm’a inzal edilen “kelimât-ı aşere”

ELMALILI:6:151/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r5.speaker: Bikâî
ELMALILI:6:151/r5.claim: Biqāʿī explains the tablets' ten commandments as prohibitions of shirk, false oath, filial impiety, murder, adultery, theft, deceit, coveting, and Sabbath disrespect, plus a Sabbath command.
ELMALILI:6:151/r5.anchor: Bunu Bikâî[^2] Mesâ‘idü’n-nazar li’l-işrâf alâ makāsıdi’s-süver nâmındaki eserinde şöyle îzah eder

ELMALILI:6:151/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r6.claim: The author counts nine listed prohibitions; tawhid is their first foundation, included in the ban on shirk and summarized earlier in the surah.
ELMALILI:6:151/r6.anchor: Görülüyor ki bu dokuzdur, bütün bunların birincisi de sûrenin başından beri îzah olunagelen îmân-ı tevhiddir

ELMALILI:6:151/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r7.claim: These ten essential rulings constitute the true religion's foundation and do not change with differences among peoples or ages.
ELMALILI:6:151/r7.anchor: ümem ü a‘sârın ihtilâfıyla ihtilâf etmeyen ahkâm-ı aşeredir

ELMALILI:6:151/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r8.claim: The prohibition of shirk bars every form of associating anything with God in belief and obeying anyone in an act of disobedience to God.
ELMALILI:6:151/r8.anchor: Allah’a herhangi bir şeyi hiçbir vechile şerîk iddia etmeyiniz, amel nokta-i nazarından Allah’a masiyet olan hususta başkasına itaat etmeyiniz

ELMALILI:6:151/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r9.claim: Ihsan toward parents means treating one's father and mother with goodness and graciousness.
ELMALILI:6:151/r9.anchor: baba ve ananıza iyilik ve güzellik ediniz

ELMALILI:6:151/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r10.claim: Although the passage introduces prohibitions, it also gives closely related commands; prohibitions can be inferred from commands.
ELMALILI:6:151/r10.anchor: maksadın yalnız muharremâtı değil, onlarla şiddet-i alâkası bulunan evâmiri de beyan olduğu anlaşılır

ELMALILI:6:151/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r11.claim: In legal theory, a command entails prohibition of its opposite when omission defeats the command's purpose; otherwise it entails disapproval.
ELMALILI:6:151/r11.anchor: bir şeyle emir zıddının tahrîmini iktizâ eder

ELMALILI:6:151/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r12.claim: The command to show parents kindness necessarily forbids hurting them; only benevolence toward them should be contemplated and done.
ELMALILI:6:151/r12.anchor: “vâlideyninize ihsan ediniz” emri “onları asla incitmeyiniz” nehyini de müstelzimdir

ELMALILI:6:151/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r13.claim: Parental kindness must not lead to shirk by obeying parents when they demand disobedience to God, as Luqman 31:15 makes explicit.
ELMALILI:6:151/r13.anchor: ana baba evlâdlarının Allah’a isyan etmesiyle memnun olacaklar ise onları bu suretle memnun etmeye çalışmak Allah’a şirk mânasında

ELMALILI:6:151/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r14.claim: Parents must preserve their children's right to life, just as children owe benevolence to their parents.
ELMALILI:6:151/r14.anchor: evlâdın hakk-ı hayâtına tecavüz etmemek, muhafaza eylemek de ebeveynin vazifesidir

ELMALILI:6:151/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r15.claim: If killing a child from actual poverty is forbidden, killing from fear of future poverty is even more plainly forbidden, as Isra 17:31 clarifies.
ELMALILI:6:151/r15.anchor: bilfiil “fakirim besleyemeyeceğim” diye evlâdı öldürmek haram olunca, fakir değil iken fakir olmak korkusu ile evlâd katletmenin haram olacağı evleviyetle âşikârdır

ELMALILI:6:151/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r16.claim: Arab polytheists buried daughters alive, through ignorant pride or poverty, with fear of poverty the predominant motive; Satan made child-killing seem attractive.
ELMALILI:6:151/r16.anchor: Arap müşrikleri kız çocuklarını diri diri kabirlere gömüyorlardı ki buna “ve’d” tâbir olunur

ELMALILI:6:151/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151/r17.claim: The ban targets the Arabs' female infanticide but its ruling also covers abortion and is not limited to them.
ELMALILI:6:151/r17.anchor: hükmünün onlara münhasır olmadığı ve çocuk düşürmek cinayetlerine dahi şâmil olduğu derkârdır

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r1.claim: Whether rich or poor and strong or weak, people must not kill children from fear that supporting them will impoverish them; God provides for both generations.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r1.anchor: gerek fakir olunuz ve gerek zengin, gerek zayıf olunuz gerek kavî, evlâda bakmakla yoksul kalmaktan korkup onları herhangi bir suretle öldürmeyiniz

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r2.claim: People should not judge themselves unable to obtain provision and commit murder, because God, not they, provides for them and their children.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r2.anchor: sizi ve onları merzuk eden, besleyen ve besleyecek olan Biziz. Yani siz değilsiniz

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r3.claim: Every kind of sexual indecency, including zina and sodomy, is forbidden in public brothels or secret liaisons, along with its preliminaries and means.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r3.anchor: zina ve livata gibi her nevi fuhşiyyât gerek erâzil-i müşrikînin yaptıkları gibi açık kârhânelerde olsun

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r4.claim: Because plural fawāḥish immediately suggests zina yet encompasses every shameful sexual act, it is broader than the singular sense of the term.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r4.anchor: “fâhişe”den mütebâdir olan zinadır. Fakat “fevâhiş” diye cem‘îrâd edilmesi zina kabîlinden olan her nevi ef‘âl-i şenî‘aya

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r5.speaker: some commentators
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r5.claim: Some exegetes interpret the open and hidden indecencies universally as sin, referring the phrase to the wording in 6:120.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r5.anchor: bazı müfessirîn bunu ale’l-umûm “ism” (اثم) ile tefsir edip

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r6.claim: The general interpretation as all sin is not evident here in light of the verse's context and transmitted reports.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r6.anchor: gerek âyetin siyâkı ve gerek rivayet nokta-i nazarından bu mâna burada pek zâhir değildir

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r7.claim: The placement of sexual indecencies between child-killing and homicide suggests a killing dimension: zina is a grave crime and its child may be exposed to death.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r7.anchor: fuhşiyyât, nefsinde bir cinâyet-i azîme olmakla beraber bir de katl-i evlâd hükmündedir

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r8.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r8.claim: The Prophet described coitus interruptus as hidden infanticide, reinforcing the killing associated with sexual wrongdoing.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r8.anchor: Nitekim Resûlullah azl hakkında bile ذلِكَ الْوَأْدُ الخَْفِ ُّي buyurmuştur

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r9.claim: A protected life is one whose blood is inviolable through Islam or covenant; killing it is forbidden except for an established right.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r9.anchor: İslâm ile olsun, ahd ile olsun demini masûn ve muhterem ve katlini haram kıldığı herhangi bir nefsi de katletmeyiniz

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r10.claim: A Prophetic report names three grounds making a Muslim's blood lawful: apostasy after faith, adultery after marriage, and unlawful homicide.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r10.anchor: Müslim bir kimsenin kanı helâl olmaz

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r11.claim: Al-Ma'idah summarizes the grounds more broadly as a life for a life or corruption on earth; its war passage further defines corruption, yielding four grounds if a Muslim commits it.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r11.anchor: Sûre-i Mâide’de ise gayr-i müslime de şâmil olmak üzere

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r12.claim: Unlike other matters, where prohibition needs separate proof, the default regarding human life is sanctity; permissibility of killing requires separate proof.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r12.anchor: Katl-i nefste asıl olan haram olmaktır. Helâl olması ayrı bir delil ile sâbit olabilir

ELMALILI:6:151#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r13.claim: God firmly enjoined these five duties with compassion and a covenant so that people reason, restrain themselves, and avoid harmful prohibitions.
ELMALILI:6:151#2/r13.anchor: Rabbiniz size tavsiye etti kemâl-i lutf u rahmetiyle müekked bir surette emr eyleyip ahid verdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.claim: After criticizing baseless polytheist rules, these verses set out nine principal divine commands on monotheism and morality, then command following God's straight path as the encompassing duty; the invitation frames these as the sole correct and obligatory way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.anchor: bu âyetlerde asıl benimsenmesi gereken başlıca ilâhî kurallar ve hükümler yer almakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r2.claim: Avoiding all association with God expresses Islam's central doctrine of divine unity and is the first condition of being Muslim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r2.anchor: Bu, İslâm’ın ana ilkesi olan Allah’ın her yönden birliği inancının bir gereği olup müslüman olmanın da ilk şartıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r3.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r3.claim: Razi lists polytheist groups discussed in the surah: idol worshippers, star worshippers, adherents of Yazdan and Ahriman as gods, and those who attribute sons or daughters to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r3.anchor: Putperestler, yıldızperestler, Yezdân ve Ehrimen’in tanrılığını iddia edenler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r4.claim: Ihsan toward parents derives from husn, meaning goodness and beautiful conduct; placing it directly after God's unity underscores parental rights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r4.anchor: Âyette bu buyruğun, Allah’ın birliğine inanmayı emreden ifadeden hemen sonra gelmesi, anne baba hakkının önemini gösterir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r5.claim: Killing children from fear of poverty implies doubt about God's abundant provision; the ban may also cover killing the unborn, not only pre-Islamic infanticide.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r5.anchor: anne karnındaki çocuğun öldürülmesinin de yasaklandığı dikkate alınmalıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r6.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r6.claim: Hadith reports say the Prophet permitted coitus interruptus, the simplest form of birth control.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r6.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in, doğum kontrolünün en basit şekli olan azil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r7.claim: Most scholars across the legal schools consider coitus interruptus permissible; this implies other non-harmful medical contraception is also allowed so long as no other prohibition is violated, since the Qur'an forbids killing a child rather than preventing conception.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r7.anchor: Çeşitli mezheplerin âlimlerinin çoğunluğu da azlin câiz olduğunu kabul etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r8.claim: Because procreation is marriage's primary purpose, arbitrary avoidance of children for beauty or convenience is improper, especially when Muslim population growth is needed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r8.anchor: kadının güzelliğinin bozulması, çocuğun bir ayak bağı telakki edilmesi gibi keyfî sebeplerle fıtratın tabii akışına müdahale etmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r9.claim: Most contemporary scholars consider abortion forbidden at every stage of pregnancy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r9.anchor: Günümüz âlimlerinin büyük çoğunluğu, hamileliğin hangi safhasında olursa olsun, çocuk düşürme ve aldırmanın haram olduğu görüşündedirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r10.speaker: İbn Abbas
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that pre-Islamic Arabs disapproved of adultery in public but practiced it secretly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r10.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan nakledilen bir rivayete göre Câhiliye Arapları açıktan zina edilmesini hoş karşılamaz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r11.claim: Because fawahish is plural and no limiting evidence identifies only adultery, the author rejects narrowing the prohibition to zina; it covers shameful speech and conduct more broadly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r11.anchor: bu yasağı zina ile sınırlamak doğru değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r12.claim: Explicitly forbidding both hidden and open wrongdoing shows that one who hides sin from people but not from God fears human censure more than God's command; forbidding even approach requires avoiding conditions that lead to sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r12.anchor: “yapmayın” veya “işlemeyin” yerine “yaklaşmayın” buyurulması, insanı kaçınılmaz olarak kötülük işlemeye sevkedebilecek ortam ve şartlardan uzak durmayı öngörmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r13.claim: The ban on killing without just cause also declares life sacred and inviolable from Adam onward; haqq means a lawful, valid reason judged right by religion and reason.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r13.anchor: insan hayatının Hz. Âdem’den beri dokunulmaz olduğunu ima eder

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.claim: Verses 145–154 recall prohibitions in Abraham’s and Moses’ religions and refute the idolaters’ claim that God ordained their path and should redirect them if He disapproves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.anchor: The things forbidden in the religion of Abraham (sws) and the religion of Moses (sws) are referred to.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.claim: The basic teachings of Abraham's religion call Quraysh to the straight path; Moses' law likewise guides its adherents to that path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.anchor: the Quraysh too are invited to this straight path. They must not deviate from them and wander in misguidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.speaker: author
