ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.claim: These verses detail Abraham's religion and expose the Quraysh's neglect of its duties to God and creatures while claiming adherence through invented food taboos; their first violation is polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.anchor: These verses state the real religion of Abraham (sws) in detail.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.claim: The passage states some duties positively and others negatively; as in 17:22–38, each form implies its opposite, such as monotheism from the ban on polytheism and kind treatment from the duty to honor parents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.anchor: Exactly the same style has been adopted in these directives in verses 22-38 of Sūrah Banī Isrā’īl.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.claim: The positive command to treat parents kindly tacitly forbids disrespect and scolding; 17:23–24 makes those implications explicit and adds tender speech and humility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.anchor: disrespect to the parents nor scold them; in fact, be kind to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.claim: Imlāq means poverty; fear of feeding and raising children must not lead to killing them, which occurred through idolatrous custom, female infanticide tied to honor, and poverty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.anchor: means “poverty.” In verse 31 of Sūrah Banī Isrā’īl

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.claim: Parents are custodians, not providers: God sustains both them and their children, so they must fulfill their duties to children according to reason and religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.anchor: It is God Who not only provides the children but also the parents.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.claim: Governments can overstep by entering God's domain, thereby acting against nature and their creator instead of benefiting citizens.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p148.anchor: instead of being beneficial to their citizens, they end up fighting against nature and their creator.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.claim: A conscientious government should develop livelihoods and educate people toward moderation and diligence, but must not impose a population quota or prevent births through birth control.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.anchor: it would be exceeding limits if a government starts ordering them to produce a certain amount of children

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.claim: Modern family planning repeats the Jāhiliyyah rationale for killing children: both assume people themselves provide sustenance and resent God's provision of children.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p149.anchor: The philosophy of both is the same: both regard themselves to be the providers of sustenance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: Vice can only be removed when it is uprooted from the heart.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: cannot be gotten rid of unless it is uprooted from the heart.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: Vice nourished through the senses and thoughts grows into a spiritual cancer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: it will continue to be nurtured through the eye, the ear, the tongue and thoughts until it becomes a spiritual cancer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: Even unacted vice can grip the mind and heart so strongly that efforts at self-cleansing fail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: Even if it may never materialize practically, it grips the mind and heart of a person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: Virtue and vice originate in the heart; vice sustained by the senses and thoughts can become spiritual cancer even without outward action, so believers must avoid inner and outer lewdness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: inner and outer forms of lewdness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: Every soul is sacred; killing is permitted under the Sharīʿah only for offenses such as murder, rebellion against God and His messenger, or adultery, and otherwise is unjustified.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: Without such offences, killing someone is not justified.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: The Quraysh abandoned Abraham's directives while claiming his religion through food taboos; the Prophet recounts them so they reconsider and understand their deviation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: the Quraysh have abandoned them and by regarding some lawful animals to be unlawful, they claim to be followers of this religion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: The sequence moves from reflection that frees one from blind following, to recalling truths of human nature, then to taqwā; Sharīʿah's fundamentals emerge from human nature when people heed God's reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: The sharī‘ah is a treasury that has been extracted from our nature and has been consigned to us

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: Just as wholesome purity distinguishes lawful food, justice, goodness, and good conventions distinguish commanded conduct from rebellion, lewdness, and vice in Abraham's and Islam's religions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: all things that are enjoined stem from justice, goodness and good conventions and all things that are forbidden stem from rebelliousness, lewdness and vice.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#4/r1.speaker: معمر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#4/r1.claim: Ma‘mar explains manifest and hidden indecencies as those done openly and secretly.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p221#4/r1.anchor: عن معمر في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ﴾ قال سرها وعلانيتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r4.claim: After describing fabricated bans and God's permitted food, the passage turns to His actual prohibitions and positive duties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r4.anchor: ما حرمه تعالى عليهم من أشياء نهاهم عنها وما أوجب عليهم من أشياء أمرهم بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r5.claim: The address in qul is to the Messenger; taʿālaw is directed either to the polytheists, as context suggests, or to everyone present, with the same ruling applying to all.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r5.anchor: والخطاب في قل للرسول وفي تعالوا قيل للمشركين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r6.claim: The command calls all people to hear the Islamic law sent for all humanity; atlu means to recite or recount in sequence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r6.anchor: أمره تعالى أن يدعو جميع الخلق إلى سماع ما حرم الله بشرع الإسلام المبعوث به إلى الأسود والأحمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r7.speaker: كعب الأحبار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r7.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says these verses open the Torah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r7.anchor: هذه الآيات مفتتح التوراة بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قل تعالوا أتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas calls them the unchanging, universally shared commandments identified as the muhkamāt in Ali ʿImran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r8.anchor: هذه الآيات هي المحكمات التي ذكرها الله في سورة آل عمران أجمعت عليها شرائع الخلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r9.claim: Another view identifies them as the Ten Commandments given to Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p684/r9.anchor: وقد قيل: إنها العشر كلمات المنزلة على موسى عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r1.claim: Mā is explained as a relative pronoun, a verbal noun meaning prohibition, or an interrogative; the interrogative reading is weak because atlu is not a verb of thought and cannot be suspended.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r1.anchor: مصدرية أي تحريم ربكم. وقيل: استفهامية منصوبة بحرم أي أي شيء حرم ربكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r2.claim: Most attach ʿalaykum to ḥarrama rather than atlu, while Ibn al-Shajari prefers attachment to atlu because it is nearer, a Kufan analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r2.anchor: وعليكم متعلق بجرم لا بأتل فهو من إعمال الثاني. وقال ابن الشجري: إن علقته بأتل فهو جيد لأنه أسبق وهو اختيار الكوفيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats an as explanatory and lā as prohibitive because recitation conveys speech and the following material is a sentence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r3.anchor: الظاهر أن أن تفسيرية ولا ناهية لأن أتل فعل بمعنى القول وما بعد أن جملة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r4.claim: Asked how positive commands can fall under what God forbids, he says they are included because their opposites are forbidden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r4.anchor: علم أن التحريم راجع إلى أضدادها وهي الإشارة إلى الوالدين وبخس الكيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan calls that account very far-fetched: the commands are not themselves forbidden, and there is no need to make their opposites part of the list.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r5.anchor: وكون هذه الأشياء اشتركت في الدخول تحت حكم التحريم وكون التحريم راجعا إلى أضداد الأوامر بعيد جدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r6.claim: The clear reading coordinates the positive commands with taʿālaw and atlu as a second instruction, leaving only the prohibitions under the explanatory an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r6.anchor: بل هي معطوفة على قوله: تعالوا أتل ما حرم أمرهم أولا بأمر يترتب عليه ذكر مناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r7.claim: A second possible reading places commands and prohibitions alike under explanatory an by supplying an understood phrase for what God commanded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p685/r7.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي وداخلة تحت أن التفسيرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r1.speaker: امرؤ القيس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r1.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays supplies an example where a positive command coordinates with a prohibition, supporting the second parsing option.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r2.claim: An may also be nominalizing, with the clause either raised after an implicit subject or placed in several possible accusative roles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r2.anchor: وقد جوزوا في أن أن تكون مصدرية لا تفسيرية في موضع رفع وفي موضع نصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r3.claim: Attaching the clause to ʿalaykum as an obligation is distant because it breaks the apparent sentence structure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r3.anchor: ويكون من باب الإغراء وتم الكلام عند قوله: أتل ما حرم ربكم أي التزموا انتفاء الإشراك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r4.claim: Reading it as a purpose clause is distant because the commands and prohibitions are both coordinated, so it cannot explain only what was prohibited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r4.anchor: وهذا بعيد لأن ما جاء بعده أمر معطوف بالواو ومناه هي معطوفة بالواو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r5.claim: Supplying an omitted verb meaning I enjoin you is also distant because ellipsis runs against the default.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r5.anchor: وهذا بعيد لأن الإضمار على خلاف الأصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r6.claim: The remaining nominalizing and substitution analyses fail to preserve the negative force of lā or wrongly confine all prohibitions to shirk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r6.anchor:
وهذان الوجهان لا فيهما زائدة كهي في قوله:
ما منعك ألا تسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why an is not treated as governing the verb and lā tushrikū as a substitute for mā ḥarrama.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r7.anchor: هلا قلت هي التي تنصب الفعل وجعلت ألا تشركوا بدلا من ما حرم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r8.claim: He answers that then all following clauses would have to be prohibitions, including the positive duties to parents, fairness, and covenant-keeping.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p686/r8.anchor: وجب أن يكون لا تشركوا ولا تقربوا ولا تقتلوا ولا تتبعوا السبل نواهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan says it is not necessary to coordinate every positive command with every prohibition: kindness to parents can attach to the initial call instead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r1.anchor: أن تكون جميع الأوامر معطوفة على جميع ما دخل عليه لا لأنا بينا جواز عطف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r2.claim: The prohibition of shirk includes worshipping idols, jinn, sons, or daughters alongside God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r2.anchor: وألا تشركوا شامل لمن أشرك بالله الأصنام كقوم إبراهيم ومن أشرك بالله الجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r3.speaker: ابن الجوزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi gives two senses of shirk: assigning God a partner or obeying someone in disobedience to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r3.anchor: ادعاء شريك لله. وقيل: طاعة غير الله في معصية الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r4.claim: The phrase about parents was explained earlier in al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r4.anchor: وتقدم تفسير وبالوالدين إحسانا في سورة البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r5.claim: Min here gives the reason for killing children: poverty; killing is forbidden except on lawful grounds, and God provides for parents and children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r5.anchor: من هنا سببية أي من فقر لقوله خشية إملاق وقتل الولد حرام إلا بحقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r6.claim: As God provides, a parent should not kill a child any more than killing oneself; the prohibition counters the gravest abuse after the command to honor parents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r6.anchor: وإذا كان هو الرازق فكما لا تقتل نفسك كذلك لا تقتل ولدك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r7.claim: A Prophetic report lists associating a partner, killing a child for fear of sharing food, and adultery with a neighbor's wife among the gravest sins; the child-killing wording is drawn from this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r7.anchor: وأن تقتل ولدك مخافة أن يطعم معك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r8.claim: This verse addresses actual poverty and reassures parents first; al-Israʾ addresses fear of future poverty and reassures them about children first, so the passages cover two distinct cases.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687/r8.anchor: فبدأ أولا بقوله: نحن نرزقكم خطابا للآباء وتبشيرا لهم بزوال الإملاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r1.claim: The visible and hidden indecencies follow the same explanation as the phrase in 6:120.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r1.anchor: المنقول فيما ظهر منها وما بطن كالمنقول في وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r2.claim: Killing is included among indecencies generally, but singled out for emphasis and because the lawful exception applies to killing specifically.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r2.anchor: هذا مندرج تحت عموم الفواحش إذ الأجود أن لا يخص الفواحش بنوع ما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r3.claim: Protected lives include believers, protected scriptural communities, and people under treaty; lawful grounds include apostasy, retaliation, adultery after marriage, and armed brigandage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r3.anchor: والنفس المحرمة هي المؤمنة والذمية والمعاهدة وبالحق بالسبب الموجب لقتلها كالردة والقصاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r4.claim: That is what He instructed refers to everything above; the wording conveys tenderness by making people God's appointed trustees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r4.anchor: أشار إلى جميع ما تقدم وفي لفظ وصاكم من اللطف والرأفة وجعلهم أوصياء له تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r5.claim: The closing call to reason asks people to grasp the benefits of these duties in religion and worldly life; waṣiyya is a firm, confirmed command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r5.anchor: لعلّكم تعقلون أي فوائد هذا التكاليف ومنافعها في الدين والدنيا والوصاة الأمر المؤكد المقرر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r6.speaker: الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r6.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line witnesses the word waṣāya for an instruction or testament.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r6.anchor: أجدك لم تسمع وصاة محمد ... نبي الإله حين أوصى وأشهدا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.claim: After exposing their false claims, the Prophet is told to invite them to hear the prohibitions the situation requires; food prohibitions were already explained, and the invitation signals that these must be avoided.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.anchor: أمر له صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ما ظهر بطلان ما ادعوا أن يبين لهم من المحرمات ما يقتضي الحال بيانه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.claim: Taʿalaw originally tells someone lower to come up from a higher place, then broadened into a general invitation; it may still imply their low station in ignorance and ascent through listening.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.anchor: والأصل فيه أن يقول من هو في مكان عال لمن هو أسفل منه ثم اتسع فيه بالتعميم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.claim: 'I will recite' answers the invitation command: if they come, the Prophet will recite to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( أتل ( جواب الأمر أي ان تأتوني أتل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.claim: What God prohibited may be a relative clause with an omitted antecedent, meaning the verses that contain the prohibition, or an interrogative object of 'prohibited' within the recitation clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.anchor: وما في قوله تعالى : ( ما حرم ربكم ( إما موصولة والعائد محذوف أي أقرأ الذي حرمه ربكم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.claim: The interrogative analysis means: come so I may tell you and explain what God has prohibited; the clause can serve as an object of recitation because recitation is a kind of saying.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.anchor: والمعنى هنا على الاستفهام تعالوا أقل لكم وأبين جواب أي شيء حرم ربكم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.claim: 'Upon you' most suitably modifies 'prohibited,' rather than 'recite,' because it emphasizes avoidance and fits the appeal to God's lordship over the listeners.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.anchor: ورجح الأول بأنه أنسب بمقام الاعتناء بإيجاب الانتهاء عن المحرمات

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r7.claim: Shirk is named first because it is the greatest prohibition and the gravest major sin; 'anything' may mean any form of association or any thing whatsoever.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r7.anchor: وبدأ سبحانه بأمر الشرك لأنه أعظم المحرمات وأكبر الكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains kindness to parents as dutifulness with gentleness: no harsh answer, hard stare, or raised voice, but humility before them like a slave before a master.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس يريد البر بهما مع اللطف ولين الجانب فلا يغلظ لهما في الجواب ولا يحد النظر إليهما

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r9.claim: The command to honor parents follows the prohibition of shirk because God's blessing is greatest and parental blessing next: God is the true cause of existence, while parents are its apparent cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r9.anchor: لأن نعمة الوالدين أعظم النعم على العبد بعد نعمة الله تعالى لأن المؤثر الحقيقي في وجود الإنسان هو الله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r10.claim: The ban on killing children concerns burying them alive from poverty or fear of poverty; some say the two verses address different groups, distinguishing current poverty from future fear, and their provision is named first accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p53#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب في كل آية لصنف وليس خطابا واحدا فالمخاطب بقوله سبحانه : ( من املاق ) من ابتلي بالفقر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r1.claim: The assurance that God provides both groups explains the prohibition, removes the claimed motive, and guarantees their livelihood.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r1.anchor: وأيا ما كان فجملة ( نحن ) الخ استئناف مسوق لتعليل النهي وإبطال سببية ما اتخذوه سببا لمباشرة المنهي عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say 'indecencies' means adultery, whether openly practiced in taverns by low-status people or secretly with lovers by elites.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r2.anchor: وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس والضحاك والسدي وقيل : المراد بها المعاصي كلها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r3.claim: Al-Razi and others interpret the indecencies as all sins and discuss several prior interpretations of outward and inward sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r3.anchor: وفي المراد بما ظهر منها وما بطن على هذا أقوال تقدمت الإشارة إليها واختار ذلك الإمام وجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r4.claim: Al-Alusi prefers adultery as the referent because it fits the sequence of neighboring prohibitions; as a grave crime, it also resembles killing offspring, since illicit children are effectively lost.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r4.anchor: ورجح بعض المحققين الأول بأنه الأوفق بنظم المتعاطفات

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r5.claim: A prophetic report calls withdrawal before conception a hidden form of burying a child alive, supporting the placement of adultery between the two killing prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r5.anchor: وقد روي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال في حق العزل : ذاك وأد خفي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r6.claim: The all-sins reading does not explain why this general prohibition is placed between two specific bans, whereas the adultery reading does; 'do not approach' intensifies deterrence or warns that approach invites commission.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r6.anchor: وعلى القول الآخر لا يظهر وجه توسيط هذا العام بين أفراده ويكون توسيطه بين النهيين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r7.claim: The protected life is one safeguarded by Islam or covenant: this excludes a hostile combatant and includes a protected non-Muslim; Ibn Jubayr's restriction to believers is misplaced.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r7.anchor: أي حرم قتلها بأن عصمها بالإسلام أو بالعهد فيخرج الحربي ويدخل الذمي فما روي عن ابن جبير

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r8.claim: 'Except by right' may qualify all circumstances, causes, or kinds of killing; the reported lawful grounds are apostasy after faith, adultery after marriage, and killing a protected person.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r8.anchor: وذلك كما روي في الخبر بالكفر بعد الإيمان والزنا بعد الإحصان وقتل النفس المعصومة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r9.claim: 'That' refers to the five weighty commands; the emphatic nominal sentence renews the covenant, while al-Razi says it makes acceptance easier by conveying gentleness and mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p54/r9.anchor: أي ما ذكر من التكاليف الخمسة الجليلة الشأن من بين التكاليف الشرعية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55/r1.claim: 'So that you reason' means using reason to restrain the self from committing forbidden, shameful acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55/r1.anchor: أي تستعملون عقولكم التي تعقل نفوسكم وتحبسها عن مباشرة القبائح المحرمة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.speaker: القطب الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.claim: Al-Qutb al-Razi says the first verse ends with 'reason' because people committed its sins heedlessly, while the second ends with 'remember' because they already practiced and took pride in its duties but might forget them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.anchor: لأن القوم كانوا مستمرين على الشرك وقتل الأولاد وقربان الزنا وقتل النفس المحرمة بغير حق غير مستنكفين ولا عاقلين قبحها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.speaker: القطب الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.claim: Asked why honoring parents, already practiced, is in the first set, al-Razi answers that parents' blessing follows God's and their care in childhood makes ingratitude especially serious.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.anchor: أعظم النعم على الإنسان نعمة الله تعالى ويتلوها نعمة الوالدين لأنهما المؤثران في الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.claim: Al-Razi instead says the first five duties are obvious and call for rational recognition, while the four later duties are subtle and require thought to find the balanced course.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.anchor: التكاليف الخمسة المذكورة في الآية الأولى ظاهرة جلية فوجب تعقلها وتفهمها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.claim: Al-Alusi suggests that the first set is mostly prohibitions, whose restraint suits the idea of reason holding one back, whereas the later commands need emphasis so they persist in memory.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.anchor: إن أكثر التكليفات الأول أدى بصيغة النهي وهو في معنى المنع والمرء حريص على ما منع

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.claim: A hasan report from Ibn Masud says whoever wishes to see the Prophet's testament bearing his seal should recite the verses beginning 'Say: come, I will recite' through 'that you may be mindful.'
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : من سره أن ينظر إلى وصية محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام بخاتمه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.claim: Ubadah reports that the Prophet sought a pledge on these three verses: fulfillment earns God's reward; a shortcoming punished in this life is expiated, while a deferred matter is left to God's choice to punish or pardon.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الآيات الثلاث ثم تلاهن إلى آخرهن

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r5.speaker: كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r5.claim: Kaʿb swears that the opening verse of these prohibitions is the first verse of the Torah, beginning with the basmala and the command to recite what God has forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r5.anchor: سمع كعب رجلا يقرأ ( قل تعالوا أتل ) الخ فقال : والذي نفس كعب بيده إنها لأول آية في التوراة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says these decisive verses have never been abrogated in any scripture, are forbidden to all humanity, are the Mother of the Book, and lead their practitioners to Paradise and abandoners to the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.anchor: هذه آيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب وهن محرمات على بني آدم كلهم وهن أم الكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.claim: The construction 'that you do not associate' may use a particle of explanation or a nominalizing particle; each choice raises syntactic and semantic objections.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.anchor: هذا و ( أن ) في قوله سبحانه ( أن لا تشركوا ) يحتمل أن تكون مفسرة وأن تكون مصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.claim: If nominalizing, the phrase seems to name the forbidden act as association rather than refraining from it, and affirmative commands then follow a negative prohibition; treating 'do not' as a relative clause was a view attributed to Sibawayh but is rejected here.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.anchor: وظاهر أن المحرم هو الاشراك لا نفيه وأن الأوامر بعد معطوفة على ( لا تشركوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari chooses the explanatory particle and includes later commands by understanding their opposites as implicit prohibitions; he connects 'this is My path' to 'follow it' with an omitted causal lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.anchor: واختار الزمخشري كونها مفسرة وعطف الأوامر لأنها معنى نواه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers the second objection by treating affirmative commands as carrying an implicit prohibition of their opposites, such as not mistreating parents, shortchanging measures, abandoning justice, or breaking covenants.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.anchor: دل على أن التحريم راجع إلى أضدادها بمعنى أن الأوامر كأنها ذكرت وقصد لوازمها التي هي النهي عن الأضداد

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says the commands may instead coordinate with 'I recite what God prohibited,' not with the prohibitions themselves, so the first clause introduces prohibitions and a second introduces commands.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.anchor: والثاني ان تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي داخلة تحت حكم التفسيرية ويصح هذا على تقدير محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.claim: Alternatively, the explanatory particle may govern an omitted 'and what He commanded,' understood from the prohibition phrase; then positive and negative commands can both be explained and coordinated.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.anchor: ان تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي داخلة تحت حكم التفسيرية ويصح هذا على تقدير محذوف تكون أن مفسرة له

ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r2.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r2.claim: Al-Tabarsi allows an omitted lām before 'that you do not associate': God explains the forbidden because people who prohibit what He made lawful treat obedience to others as equal to obedience to God and become polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r2.anchor: ونقل الطبرسي جواز كون ( أن لا تشركوا ) بتقدير اللام على معنى أبين لكم الحرام

ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r3.claim: Al-Alusi says the Qur'an should not be construed by this strained grammatical analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r3.anchor: ولا ينبغي تخريج كلام الله تعالى على مثل ذلك كما لا يخفى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r1.claim: When asked what God prohibited, the Prophet is to recite the certain, true prohibitions rather than the conjectures and lies his opponents claim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم ألا تشركوا به شيئا} وذلك أنهم سألوا وقالوا:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r2.claim: The wording appears to say God forbids not associating, though the forbidden act is shirk; one parsing makes an nominative, meaning the prohibition is that they not associate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r2.anchor: فإن قيل: ما معنى قوله "حرم ربكم عليكم ألا تشركوا به شيئا" والمحرم هو الشرك لا ترك الشرك؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r3.claim: An alternative accusative parsing treats lā as extra, like the cited verse, so the sense is that God forbade associating; another stops after your Lord has forbidden and treats do not associate as an independent exhortation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: محله نصب، واختلفوا في وجه انتصابه، قيل: معناه حرم عليكم أن تشركوا به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the construction can follow its sense: recite the prohibition of shirk, or command the audience not to associate anything with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: يجوز أن يكون هذا محمولا على المعنى، أي: أتل عليكم تحريم الشرك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r5.claim: Show kindness to parents; do not kill children from poverty because God provides for parents and children; avoid indecencies both public and secret.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r5.anchor: {وبالوالدين إحسانا ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق} فقر، {نحن نرزقكم وإياهم} أي: لا تئدوا بناتكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r6.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs condemned public adultery but accepted it in secret; God prohibited both forms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r6.anchor: وكان أهل الجاهلية يستقبحون الزنا في العلانية ولا يرون به بأسا في السر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says manifest indecency means wine and hidden indecency means adultery.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p202#2/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ما ظهر: الخمر، وما بطن: الزنا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r1.claim: The sanctified life includes believers and protected non-Muslims; killing is lawful only for a valid cause such as apostasy, retaliation, or adultery warranting stoning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r1.anchor: {ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق} حرم الله تعالى قتل المؤمن والمعاهد إلا بالحق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet's rule that a Muslim who professes the testimony may be killed only for adultery while married, life for life, or abandoning religion and the community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says these commands are fixed in all scriptures, never abrogated, prohibited to all humanity, and are the Mother of the Book; whoever follows them enters Paradise and whoever abandons them enters Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذه الآيات محكمات في جميع الكتب، لم ينسخهن شيء

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r1.claim: Taʿālaw originally invites someone below to come up from someone above, then broadened to a general invitation; utlu means recite.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r1.anchor: أمر من التعالي وأصله أن يقوله من كان في علو لمن كان في سفل فاتسع فيه بالتعميم. { اتل } أقرأ.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r2.claim: Mā ḥarrama may be a relative, verbal noun, or interrogative object of ḥarrama; as object of utlu, the verb means say what God prohibited.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r2.anchor: منصوب بأتل وما تحتمل الخبرية والمصدرية، ويجوز أن تكون استفهامية منصوبة بحرم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r3.claim: An lā tushrikū may be parsed as a prohibition coordinated with commands; the particle may be verbal noun, warning, apposition, genitive with implicit lām, or nominative statement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r3.anchor: أي لا تشركوا به ليصح عطف الأمر عليه، ولا يمنعه تعليق الفعل المفسر

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r4.claim: Shayʾan may be a verbal noun or direct object; the positive command to treat parents well emphasizes that merely refraining from harm is insufficient.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r4.anchor: يحتمل المصدر والمفعول. { وبالولدين إحسنا } أي وأحسنوا بهما إحسانا

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r5.claim: Imlāq means poverty or fear of poverty, as in al-Isra; God's provision for parents and children refutes the motive for killing them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r5.anchor: من أجل فقر ومن خشية. كقوله: خشية إملق

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r6.claim: Fawāḥish means major sins or fornication; what is open and hidden apposes it, as in the verse about outward and inward sin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r6.anchor: كبائر الذنوب أو الزنا. { ما ظهر منها وما بطن } بدل منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r7.claim: The protected life may be killed only by lawful retaliation, execution for apostasy, or stoning of a married adulterer; the commands aim to guide reason.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:151/r7.anchor: كالقود وقتل المرتد ورجم المحصن. { ذلكم } إشارة إلى ما ذكر مفصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r1.claim: After exposing the false foundations of the polytheists’ prohibitions, the verse announces the true religion: only the Creator and sovereign may declare what is forbidden.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r2.claim: “Come” calls listeners upward from ignorance and imitation to knowledge and good conduct; al-Zamakhshari says this once-special expression became common, even for a lower-status speaker addressing a superior.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r2.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : هو من الخاص الذي صار عاما , يعني حتى صار يقوله الأسفل للأعلى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r3.claim: The author glosses “I recite” as reading, from the root of recitation in which letters follow one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r3.anchor: من التلاوة وهي اتباع بعض الحروف بعضا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r4.claim: The prohibitions are put first because they matter most, and the verse begins with exclusive worship: removing vice precedes acquiring virtue.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r5.claim: Worship is paired with kindness to parents as gratitude to benefactors; killing children follows as the gravest wrong after shirk, beginning with the especially heinous motive of fearing poverty.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r5.anchor: وقرن به البر لأنهما من باب شكر المنعم وتعظيما لأمر العقوق , ثم أولاه القتل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r6.claim: The verse names God’s provision for the already poor parents first, then for their children, because the killing is driven by present poverty.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r6.anchor: بالخطاب , أي أيها الفقراء , ثم عطف عليه الأبناء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r7.claim: The verse’s commands also prohibit their opposites, so kindness is doubly reinforced by both an explicit command and an implicit ban on mistreatment.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p740/r7.anchor: وكذا جميع المأمورات ساقها هذا السياق المفهم لأن أضدادها منهي عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r1.claim: Unlike this verse’s present-poverty wording, 17:31 describes parents who fear future poverty despite current means; Abu Hayyan notes that 17:31 therefore names the children’s provision first.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r1.anchor: أن الآباء موسرون ولكنهم يخشون من إطعام الأبناء الفقر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r2.claim: The ban on approaching grave indecencies is stronger than merely banning their commission, and “open or hidden” makes it comprehensive.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r2.anchor: وعظم أمرها بالنهي عن القربان فضلا عن الغشيان

BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r3.claim: The general ban on indecencies is followed by a specific prohibition of unlawful killing, with the exception restricted to an unmistakable, fully justified legal ground.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r4.claim: Child-killing is forbidden three times in the passage; the closing “He has charged you” names these commands and prohibitions’ opposites as divine counsel, reinforced so people may reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p741/r4.anchor: ولما كانت هذه الأشياء شديدة على النفس , ختمها بما لا يقوله إلا المحب الشفوق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.claim: The rulings are distributed across three verses, each ending with “He has charged you,” strengthening the instruction and inviting acceptance.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.anchor: وفصل ما هنا من الأحكام في ثلاث آيات , وختم كل آية لذلك بالوصية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.claim: The closing appeals progress from reason to remembrance to taqwa: reason calls for reflection, which leads to precaution against straying and ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.anchor: لأنه إذا كان العقل دعا إلى التذكير فحمل على التقوى

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r1.claim: The Qur’an was usually revealed five verses at a time, but al-An‘am descended all at once with a thousand angels, seventy from each heaven; its recitation heals the ill.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: أنزل القرآن خمسا خمسا ومن حفظ خمسا خمسا

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r2.claim: Al-An‘am descended to the Prophet as a whole, accompanied by seventy thousand angels praising and glorifying God.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r2.anchor: عن أبي كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنزلت علي سورة الأنعام جملة واحدة

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.claim: Al-An‘am was revealed in Mecca as a whole except these three verses, which were revealed in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سورة الأنعام نزلت بمكة جملة واحدة فهي مكية إلا ثلاث آيات

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r4.claim: A weakly transmitted prophetic report promises Paradise to whoever loves and recites al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r4.anchor: عن أنس مرفوعا ينادي مناديا: قارىء سورة الأنعام هلم إلى الجنة

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r5.claim: The whole sura descended at once, escorted and surrounded by five hundred angels.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: نزلت سورة الأنعام كلها جملة معها خمسمائة ملك

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r6.speaker: أبو جحيفة
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r6.claim: Al-An‘am descended all together with seventy thousand angels and was Meccan except 6:111.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r6.anchor: عن أبي جحيفة قال: نزلت سورة الأنعام جميعا معها سبعون ألف ملك كلها مكية

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r7.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r7.claim: When al-An‘am descended, the Prophet glorified God and said so many angels had escorted it that they filled the horizon.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن المنكدر قال: لما نزلت سورة الأنعام سبح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.claim: Al-An‘am descended all at once with ranks of angels stretching from the lowest heaven to earth; it was Meccan except 6:151–153.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.anchor:
عن شهر بن
حوشب قال: نزلت الأنعام جملة واحدة معها رجز من الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r9.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r9.claim: Al-An‘am descended all together accompanied by seventy thousand angels.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r9.anchor: عن عطاء قال: أنزلت الأنعام جميعا ومعها سبعون ألف ملك

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r10.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r10.claim: The sura was revealed in Mecca except 6:91, revealed in Medina concerning a Jewish man who said God had revealed nothing to any human.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r10.anchor: عن الكلبي قال: نزلت الأنعام كلها بمكة إلا آيتين نزلتا بالمدينة في رجل من اليهود

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.claim: The Prophet’s sealed testament is found in the three concluding commandments of al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: من سره أن ينظر إلى وصية محمد التي عليها خاتما

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.claim: The Prophet sought a pledge to uphold these three verses: fulfillment earns reward, while shortcoming may be punished in life or left to God’s will in the afterlife.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الآيات الثلاث

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.claim: When asked for a written sheet bearing the Prophet’s seal, al-Rabi‘ recited these concluding verses from al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.anchor: قال الربيع بن خيثم: أيسرك أن تلقى صحيفة من محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بخاتم

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.claim: Ka‘b says the first ten revealed verses of the Torah are these ten commandments at the end of al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.anchor: عن كعب قال: أول ما نزل من التوراة عشر آيات

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.claim: Ka‘b swears that the first verse in the Torah is the opening of these commandments from al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.anchor: عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عدي بن الخيار قال: سمع كعب رجلا يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.claim: Asked for advice, al-Rabi‘ wrote down the three commandments at the end of al-An‘am and told the questioner to adhere to them.
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.anchor: عن مزاحم بن زفر قال: قال رجل للربيع بن خيثم: أوصني

DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.claim: At Mina, the Prophet invited an Arab tribe to affirm God’s oneness, recognize his messengership, and shelter and defend him; he recited these commandments, then 16:90. Mafruq praised their noble morals and Hani‘ approved his words.
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادعوكم إلى شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

DURR-FULL:v3p382/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r3.claim: The Prophet foretold that God would give the tribe the Persians’ lands, wealth, rivers, and women, and asked whether they would then glorify and sanctify God.
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r3.anchor: ثم قال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن لم تلبثوا إلا يسيرا حتى يمنحكم الله بلادهم

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r1.claim: The Prophet quoted 33:45 in his conversation with the tribe at Mina and then departed holding Abu Bakr’s hand.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r1.anchor: فتلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r2.claim: Killing children ‘from poverty’ means killing them out of fear of destitution; people of the Jāhiliyya feared poverty and captivity for their daughters.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق} قال: من خشية الفاقة

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r3.claim: The apparent and hidden indecencies are what is done openly and secretly.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r3.anchor: ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن} قال: سرها وعلانيتها

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r4.claim: ‘From poverty’ means fear of poverty; the verse prohibits both secret and public adultery, which people had treated differently before Islam.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق} قال: خشية الفقر

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r5.claim: The apparent indecency is public conduct and the hidden indecency is secret conduct.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها} قال: العلانية

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r6.claim: The Prophet calls adultery, theft, and drinking wine indecencies that carry punishment.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r6.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أرأيتم الزاني والسارق

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r7.speaker: ابن أبي حازم الرهاوي
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r7.claim: Asking people for things is one of the indecencies God forbids.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r7.anchor: عن ابن أبي حازم الرهاوي أنه سمع مولاه يقول: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r8.speaker: يحيى بن جابر
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r8.claim: One forbidden indecency is a man divorcing a woman without cause after she has borne him a child.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r8.anchor: عن يحيى بن جابر قال: بلغني من الفواحش التي نهى الله عنها في كتابه

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r9.claim: Public indecencies include marrying mothers and daughters; hidden indecency means adultery.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها} قال: نكاح الأمهات والبنات

DURR-FULL:v3p383/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r10.claim: Public indecency means wronging people, while hidden indecency includes adultery and theft.
DURR-FULL:v3p383/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها} قال: ظلم الناس

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r1.claim: The prohibited life is the life of a believer, whose killing is forbidden except by right.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {ولا تقتلوا النفس} يعني نفس المؤمن

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r2.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet identified four prohibitions: associating partners with God, unlawful killing, adultery, and theft.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r2.anchor: عن سلمة بن قيس الأشجعي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع ألا إنما هي أربع

TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that anyone wishing to see the page bearing Muḥammad's seal should recite the commandments from 6:151 through 6:153; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan gharīb.
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلَى الصَّحِيفَةِ الَّتِي عَلَيْهَا خَاتَمُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلْيَقْرَأْ هَذِهِ الآيَاتِ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses إملاق as fear of poverty and adduces a poem about generosity despite poverty.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: مخافة الفقر. واستشهد بقول الشاعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r3.claim: Bint al-Shati compares the two child-killing verses: 6:151 says مِن إملاق, while 17:31 says خشية إملاق; Bukhari links the root to spending or loss of wealth, and Abu Ubayda glosses it as poverty.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p427/r3.anchor: والذي قاله أبو عبيدة في {وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ} أي من ذهاب مال.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.claim: As support, he says وصّى is used for religious matters and أوصى for worldly matters such as inheritance, with prayer and alms in 19:31 as the sole religious exception; he also compares كرّم/أكرم.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.anchor: يستعمل وصّى في أمور الدين وأوصى في أمور الدنيا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.claim: The Qur'an's commands and recommendations about goodness, prayer, and care speak of الوالدين, not الأبوين; he illustrates this with 17:23, 4:36, and 6:151.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.anchor: لا تجد في القرآن الكريم البر أو الدعاء أو التوصية إلا بذكر الوالدين لا الأبوين

ITQAN:v1p115/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p115/r5.speaker: كعب
ITQAN:v1p115/r5.claim: Another report from Ka'b says the first revelation in the Torah was ten verses from al-An'am, beginning with the call to recite what God forbade.
ITQAN:v1p115/r5.anchor: وأخرج من وجه آخر عنه قال أول ما أنزل في التوراة

ITQAN:v1p115/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p115/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
ITQAN:v1p115/r6.claim: Abu Ubayd also transmits from Ka'b that ten verses from al-An'am were first revealed in the Torah; some explain them as containing the ten commandments given to Moses, including monotheism and prohibitions of idolatry, false oath, disobedience, murder, adultery, theft, false witness, coveting, and Sabbath violation.
ITQAN:v1p115/r6.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد عنه قال أول ما أنزل الله في التوراة عشر آيات من سورة الأنعام

ITQAN:v2p501/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p501/r2.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p501/r2.claim: One analysis takes لا in ألا تشركوا as a negative particle.
ITQAN:v2p501/r2.anchor: فقيل لا نافية وقيل ناهية وقيل زائدة

ITQAN:v2p501/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p501/r3.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p501/r3.claim: Another analysis takes لا in ألا تشركوا as a prohibitive particle.
ITQAN:v2p501/r3.anchor: فقيل لا نافية وقيل ناهية وقيل زائدة

ITQAN:v2p501/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p501/r4.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p501/r4.claim: A third analysis treats لا in ألا تشركوا as extra.
ITQAN:v2p501/r4.anchor: فقيل لا نافية وقيل ناهية وقيل زائدة

ITQAN:v3p6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the final three verses of al-An'am are clear, beginning with قل تعالوا.
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وغيره عن ابن عباس قال

ITQAN:v3p6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas locates three clear verses at قل تعالوا and three more at وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه.
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من وجه آخر عن ابن عباس

ITQAN:v2p530/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p530/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p530/r1.claim: Qur'anic parsing should avoid far-fetched, weak, or anomalous constructions and prefer likely, strong, eloquent analyses; list plausible options only when no reading clearly predominates, and without forcing them.
ITQAN:v2p530/r1.anchor: الرابع أن يتجنب الأمور البعيدة والأوجه الضعيفة واللغات الشاذة ويخرج على القريب والقوي والفصيح

ITQAN:v2p530/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p530/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p530/r5.claim: Taking عليه in فلا جناح عليه أن يطوف as an exhortation after pausing at جناح is weak because exhorting an absent person is weak; the same analysis is eloquent in عليكم ألا تشركوا, addressed directly.
ITQAN:v2p530/r5.anchor: لأن إغراء الغائب ضعيف بخلاف القول
